picks.headline: No. 13 Texas Tech vs. No. 22 Arizona Football Game Preview and Prediction
picks.blurb: No. 13 Texas Tech vs. No. 22 Arizona Football Game Preview and Prediction Skip to main content SI.COM Texas Tech Athletics Texas Tech hosts Arizona in this big time Big 12 showdown. The Texas Tech Red Raiders need to focus on boosting their offense for this one. Quarterback Will Hammond has 1,561 passing yards, but he has thrown only six touchdowns and has six interceptions on the season. Explosive running back J'Koby Williams has 619 rushing yards and 5 TDs, but if you take away the Arizona State and Oregon State games, he has been inconsistent for the Red Raiders this season. Kenny Johnson , a receiver, is the main downfield target but only has one touchdown reception this season and, besides the Houston and Arizona State games, has not had a significant impact on the Texas Tech passing attack. All three as well as some other key offensive players need to step up and have big games against Arizona to win this game. The defense has to get back to focusing and dominating like they have for a lot of the season. The Red Raiders have one of the most ball-hawking secondary units in the country, sitting near the top of NCAA FBS with 13 interceptions. Defensive lineman A.J. Holmes Jr. anchors the front seven and has 6 sacks this season. However, the Red Raiders are coming off their first loss of the season, a 37-24 loss to Cincinnati where they gave up 427 yards and gave up four passing touchdowns. They will be seeking to bounce back at home to stay undefeated at home this season. Arizona, on the other hand, has a five-game winning streak and defeated Cincinnati by a final score of 34-7. Their only loss of the season was to BYU on the road. Veteran quarterback Noah Fifita leads the Arizona Wildcats, who again have a high-efficiency passing offense, with Fifiti already having 2,064 passing yards and 18 TDs through seven games. Kedrick Reescano leads the ground game with just over 300 rushing yards and five touchdowns, while wideout Isaiah Mizell is an explosive playmaker with 493 yards and 5 TDs this season, most of which have come in the Wildcats' last two games against Iowa State and West Virginia. Linebacker Taye Brown has a team-leading 27 tackles and leads the Wildcats defense. Edge rusher Chase Kennedy leads the team in pressure rate with 4 sacks, and the Texas Tech offensive line has a tough task trying to stop him from getting to the quarterback. Arizona has a scoring defense that gives up only 16.7 points per game, but they did give up 31 points against West Virginia. Arizona recently crushed Iowa State 39-3 and has put up a total of just over 200 points in their last five games. The Wildcats are also 2-1 on the road this season heading into Lubbock for this top 25 game. The key matchup for this game will be Noah Fifita vs. the Texas Tech secondary. Fifita’s efficient throwing (almost 74% completion rate) will face immediate tests from a Red Raider defense that excels at creating takeaways via interceptions. Another major matchup in this game pits the Red Raiders offensive line against Arizona’s front seven on defense. Texas Tech’s running offense behind J’Koby Williams and Quinten Joyner will face a challenge against an Arizona front seven that is holding opponents under 110 rushing yards per game. This game also has Big 12 Championship ramifications since both teams are deadlocked at 3-1 in conference play behind undefeated Utah, and the winner is squarely in the race for a Big 12 Championship Game berth. An early game prediction for this game that may change slightly as the injury reports for both teams come out later this week, but the Red Raiders bounce back and win a very close game by a final score of Texas Tech 28, Arizona 27. There's a monster Big 12 matchup on Halloween as Arizona heads to Texas Tech for a game between two 6-1 squads that will inevitably shake up the standings. My Arizona vs. Texas Tech prediction questions Will Hammond's quality, and the best of my college football picks takes a look at a total of 54.5 that might be too high. This game will be broadcast on ESPN at 12 p.m. ET on Saturday, Oct. 31. TOP PICK Who will win Arizona vs Texas Tech: Arizona +3.5 Play Arizona at anything +3 or above. Texas Tech has a quarterback problem. Will Hammond has 13 turnover-worthy passes to pair with only eight big-time throws (per PFF), and his limitations have resulted in the third least-explosive passing attack in the nation . That makes them one-dimensional offensively, and it plays into Arizona's run-stopping defense. The Red Raiders don't block well enough up front (118th in front seven havoc allowed) to compensate for the quarterback deficiency. Tech's secondary has been hit for 266.1 passing yards per game, so the Wildcats (10th in passing success rate) will be able to chuck it around. Arizona vs Texas Tech Over/Under pick: Under 54.5 Tech's offensive limitations will show through in this matchup. Arizona's defense (14th in EPA per play, 11th in success rate) is much better than the market is accounting for, as it doesn't have name recognition but is well-coordinated under Danny Gonzales. On the flip side, Tech's defense checks in at 16th in EPA per play allowed and 10th in PFF's team defense grade. The strength of this team still resides on that side of the ball, and Joey McGuire will attempt to lean on that unit and minimize possessions for Fifita. Arizona's top three wide receivers have all been out. Tre Spivey is done for the year, while Giovanni Richardson and Chris Hunter III are considered questionable. The Wildcats can still move the ball in the air, but the efficiency won't be at its peak given the cluster injuries. Arizona vs Texas Tech combo Arizona got off to slow starts against Washington State and Northern Illinois, and could do so again during a difficult trip to Lubbock. Texas Tech has cashed the First Half Under in eight of its last 13 games. Given Hammond's turnover-prone ways and overall offensive issues, the defense should be the focal point over the second half of the season. Pete Fiutak Tue, October 27, 2026 at 11:28 PM UTC · 3 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads Texas Tech was cruising right along, looking like the star of the Big 12 again after a 53-25 blowout over Arizona State, and then it walked into a wall at Cincinnati, losing with a 37-24 thud. Arizona has been fantastic ever since its 28-17 loss at BYU early in the season, including a 34-7 win over Cincinnati. But it still has a few nasty games to go in November. Both teams are 6-1. The winner will be set up nicely for a College Football Playoff spot if it doesn't win the Big 12 title. The loser will still be alive for the CFP if it wins out, but getting to the Big 12 Championship in a loaded conference season will be tough. Arizona vs Texas Tech: Quick Hits Texas Tech still has to go to Oklahoma State, but it doesn't have to face BYU or Utah, and the other three games against West Virginia, at Baylor, and TCU aren't bad. Arizona gets three of its final four games at home, getting TCU and Utah next before going to Kansas State and finishing up against Arizona State. Texas Tech won the most recent matchup 28-22 in 2024 and is 5-2-1 in the series going back to 1975. How To Watch Arizona vs Texas Tech Arizona at Texas Tech Date: Saturday, October 31, 2026 Game Time: 12:00 PM ET TV: ESPN Location: Galaxy Stadium, Lubbock, TX – Week 9 Schedule, Game Previews – CFN Top 25 | Bowl Projections – Predicting the First CFP Top 25 – CFN Week 9 Expert Picks Why Arizona Will Win For the second time all year, Texas Tech played someone who could run well, and Cincinnati went off in the 13-point win. Houston can run. It ran 37 times for 175 yards against the Red Raiders, and lost when it couldn't hit a late two-point conversion. Cincinnati wasn't exactly more physical, but it found space on the way to a 255-yard day with big run after big run. Arizona's running game isn't a killer, but it's more than effective enough, working hand-in-hand with super-accurate quarterback Noah Fifita and an offense that's great at keeping the chains moving. Why Texas Tech Will Win Arizona doesn't take the ball away enough, and that matters in a huge way here. The Wildcats forced two takeaways in the win over Washington State, and two more in the win over West Virginia. That's about it, coming up with six on the year. Texas Tech has a huge problem with turnovers, with three against Cincinnati, two against Houston, and ten in the last five games. Don't turn it over, or at least stay even in the mistake battle, and the Red Raiders should be fine. Texas Tech has a great balance to its attack, and it needs to mix it up. BYU and West Virginia – in very different ways – both showed it's possible to move the ball efficiently against the Wildcat defense. Arizona vs Texas Tech Prediction, Betting Lines Is Arizona ready to show that it's really and truly a player, or will Texas Tech wipe away the Cincinnati loss like it was just a blip? It'll be a little of both, as Arizona controls the clock and tempo for the first half, but Texas Tech gets the pass rush working early in the second half. It'll be rough for the Red Raiders without pressuring Fifita, and they won't do enough of it over the final ten minutes. Score prediction for Arizona game Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads Things have taken quite the turn for the Texas Tech football team after suffering its first loss of the season. Getting bested by Cincinnati for 60 minutes has put the Red Raiders in a pressure point. There's little wiggle room left for Joey McGuire's team to keep its hopes of repeating as Big 12 Conference champions alive. Now they have a talented Arizona team coming to Galaxy Stadium looking to kick the Red Raiders while they're down. What will it take for Texas Tech to walk away with the win? Is Arizona actually the favorite in this game? Our breakdown of the game, plus a score prediction. What's holding Texas Tech football back? It's a layered conversation as to what is keeping the Red Raiders from reaching their potential. For starters, the offense, led by quarterback Will Hammond, hasn't put up the kind of numbers Tech fans want. Receivers have struggled to get open (besides Kenny Johnson) and when they do create separation from their defenders, Hammond hasn't found them or delivered solid throws enough to take advantage. While the rushing game has been a point of scorn for some fans, J'Koby Williams has been electric, and Cameron Dickey is on track to rejoin him in the backfield this week. Defensively, the pass defense has been sporadic. The 13 interceptions (second in the nation) and five pick-6s count, but when those haven't come, opponents have had little trouble moving the ball through the air against the Red Raiders. These things have been present all year but only came to a head against Cincinnati. Now they face an Arizona team equipped to exploit these very issues. TEMPE, ARIZONA - NOVEMBER 25: Quarterback Noah Fifita #11 of the Arizona Wildcats walks out to the field before the NCAAF game against the Arizona State Sun Devils at Mountain America Stadium on November 25, 2023 in Tempe, Arizona. (Photo by Christian Petersen/Getty Images) What Arizona football can do to beat Texas Tech football The Wildcats rank sixth in the nation in total sacks (24.0), bringing constant pressure to opposing quarterbacks to get them out of rhythm. Cincinnati generated a season-high four sacks against the Red Raiders last week, while Arizona has three games with five or more sacks. Noah Fifita and the Arizona offense have also been operating at a high level, generating at least 280 yards through the air in six of the team's seven games. Fifita ranks third in the Big 12 with 2,064 passing yards, totaling 18 touchdowns to just four interceptions. The Wildcats have been hit with injuries to their receiving room, having already lost Tre Spivey for the season and seeing two others on the team's first availability report for the game. Even so, Arizona's offense has operated at a high level. Texas Tech football's notable streak on the line The Red Raiders have won their last 12 home games, which ranks one shy of the program record set during World War II when the Red Raiders won 13 straight games from 1939 to 1942. Score prediction for Texas Tech football vs. Arizona Arizona 35, Texas Tech 21: This is a pivot point for the Red Raiders to determine where they'll be in the Big 12 title race. Problem is, Texas Tech struggled to generate offense against a bad Cincinnati defense, and Arizona's defense has been quality all season. Bad recipe. But now comes the Wildcats’ toughest test since Week 2, a trip to Lubbock to take on No. 13 Texas Tech. The Red Raiders (6-1, 3-1 Big 12) are coming off a 37-24 loss at Cincinnati, whom the UA beat 34-7 at home on Oct. 3. How will the Wildcats do in this West Texas showdown? Our staff makes its predictions. Kim Doss — Texas Tech wins 28-27 Arizona has one of the top offenses in the country, landing in the top 50 in a number of categories: 2 nd in completion percentage (.738), 3 rd in third down conversion percentage (.547), 28 th in first downs, 42 nd in red zone offense (.889), 21 st in scoring offense (36.1), 12 th in team passing efficiency (169.66), and 17 th in total offense (459.4). When looking through the offensive stats, a comp for this game starts to come into focus. Houston keeps popping up in a similar position for most categories. The stats are not identical, and each team has a few strengths that the other lacks, but overall, they are fairly comparable offenses. That is relevant this week because the Cougars are the only ranked team that this week’s opponent has faced. Texas Tech took on No. 18 Houston the third week of the season. Like Saturday’s contest, it was played in Lubbock. The Red Raiders squeaked out a 28-26 win. They won their next three games handily against lesser competition before the surprising blowout upset by Cincinnati last week. It all suggests that TTU can be pushed, and perhaps even be beaten, in its home stadium. Arizona has the offense to compete. It showed last week that it can utterly shut down a team that averages just under 26 points per game. The Wildcats won’t hold TTU to three points, but they are good enough to keep this one up for grabs until the end. Ezra Amacher — Arizona wins 27- 24 Arizona is walking into a hornet’s nest in Lubbock after Texas Tech got embarrassed Cincinnati. One of the major storylines in college football this week is whether Texas Tech billionaire booster Cody Campbell is going force any personnel issues if the Red Raiders’ struggles persist. Everyone in a 100-mile radius of Lubbock knows that there is a lot more on the line Saturday than your typical Big 12 game. Another Texas Tech loss would knock the Red Raiders out of playoff contention. All that setup is to say that Arizona is facing a team that will be playing with its pants on fire. Even so, I think Noah Fifita does enough for the Wildcats to pull off one of the program’s biggest wins of the last decade. Texas Tech on paper has one of the top defenses in the Big 12, but the unit hasn’t totally lived up to the billing. Texas Tech gives up 266 passing yards per game, which is third-worst in the conference. Arizona’s passing offense is one of the best in the country, and with the Wildcats getting more receivers reps each game, I feel confident that they can successfully throw the ball Saturday. Arizona’s biggest obstacle to winning will be converting scoring opportunities on offense and limited the Red Raiders offense when they get down the field. Texas Tech’s opponents have scored on 83% of red zone drives, which is also third-worst in the Big 12. By contrast, Arizona’s red zone defense is first in the Big 12, allowing points on 67% of drives. I expect the red zone advantage to favor Arizona, allowing the Wildcats to leave Lubbock with a close win. Adam Green — Texas Tech wins 34 -24 I’d feel better had Tech not lost to Cincinnati last week. On paper Texas Tech has a better (or at least more expensive) roster. This game is in Lubbock, and it is also on Halloween. Aside from what happens on the field, there is plenty surrounding this matchup that just gives the vibe of there potentially being too much to overcome for Arizona. That said, the small spread and general vibe around each program lends itself to the idea that Arizona could leave that game Saturday with a victory and a clear path to the Big 12 title game. If Arizona can win the turnover battle and limit big plays from Tech there is then reason to believe that Noah Fifita and the Wildcats offense can move the ball. Not settling for field goal attempts will be important, of course. So yeah, Arizona could win this game. The Cats are playing excellent football and are no doubt confident they can win a big matchup on the road. But in my mind the home team will come out focused and fired up following its first loss and the environment will be such that the visitors cannot afford a slow start or to make mistakes. Asking any team to play a perfect game to have a chance to win is both unfair and unrealistic, which is why I just can’t predict an upset in this one. Juan Serrano — Texas Tech wins 31-27 It isn’t unrealistic to think that Arizona can win in Lubbock, this is a team playing with a high level of confidence and execution of its game plan. Led by Noah Fifita , the offense is moving the ball with ease and scoring almost whenever it wants to. While it is still lacking explosiveness, the run game is coming on slowly. However, this is a Red Raiders defense that is very opportunistic and athletic. It forces its opponents into mistakes that aren’t usually made. If Arizona can keep it clean on offense it will have a chance to win the game. The defense plays a lot better inside Casino Del Sol Stadium and it showed last week. Now on the road at Lubbock, it will face a challenge similar to what it saw in Provo. If the Wildcats are going to be in a position to win they will need force turnovers. Arizona only had two interceptions and five fumbles on the season, that number will need to rise on Saturday. If this game was being played in Tucson I’d probably be rolling with the Wildcats. It’s not a long road trip to Lubbock but it will end up feeling like a long trip. Texas Tech will rebound from the loss to Cincinnati with a win over Arizona. Brandon Combs — Arizona wins 31-21 I’m going to go against my pre-season prediction and my better judgement here. This is 100% a game Arizona can win, and I think they do on Saturday. Texas Tech’s defense is legit. Ben Roberts and Austin Romaine are phenomenal linebackers, combining for 102 tackles, 10 TFL, 2 sacks and 3 interceptions on the year. John Curry and Brice Pollock are fantastic cover corners. AJ Holmes is a monster on the interior defensive line and leads the conference with 5.5 sacks on the year. So why would I pick Arizona? It’s because the Red Raider offense leaves a lot to be desired. Quarterback Will Hammond has not been great this season. He is completing 68% of his passes and only has 6 touchdown passes to go along with 6 picks. Hammond can make plays with his legs but I don’t foresee Arizona’s defense having an issue there. They do have some good running backs with J’koby Williams , Quinten Joyner and Cameron Dickey . Williams is sitting at a measly 7.2 yards per carry on the season and has 619 yards on the ground and 5 touchdowns to his name. Coy Eakin and Kenny Johnson are Tech’s top two receivers, with Johnson sitting just under 500 yards and a touchdown. With all that, I believe the Arizona defense can stymy the Red Raider offense. The key will be how Noah Fifita and Seth Doege plan and execute around Tech’s solid defense. Last week showed that this defense can be taken advantage of and can be scored on. If Noah plays a clean game, I don’t see how Tech can win against the Wildcat defense. Brian Pedersen — Texas Tech wins 24-20 Arizona has a 5-game win streak in consecutive seasons for the first time since 1992-93, but the difference between this year’s run and the one in 2025 is when it has happened. Last fall the Wildcats shook off back-to-back heartbreaking losses to BYU and Houston to catch fire and win out the rest of the regular season, while this time around the solid play has been happening pretty much from the outset. But Texas Tech is far better than any of the teams the UA faced during the win streak, even the Cincinnati team that beat the Red Raiders. Tech has won 12 in a row in Lubbock, where offensive coordinator Seth Doege will be returning to his old stomping grounds. And the opponent has a very high-priced roster, one that to this point hasn’t lived up to expectations. This is a game that Arizona can’t afford to fall behind by two scores in, which means keeping mistakes to a minimum. Assuming Noah Fifita has his patented solid performance, this will come down to who capitalizes on their chances the most. picks.headline: Texas Tech vs. Arizona: Prediction, Pick and Preview
picks.blurb: Arizona vs. Texas Tech Prediction, Pick and Odds for Week 9 Teams Arizona Wildcats Arizona State Sun Devils Cincinnati Bearcats Colorado Buffaloes Houston Cougars Iowa State Cyclones Kansas Jayhawks Kansas State Wildcats Oklahoma State Cowboys TCU Horned Frogs Texas Tech Red Raiders West Virginia Mountaineers Former Foes Missouri Tigers Nebraska Cornhuskers Oklahoma Sooners Texas A&M Aggies Texas Longhorns Recruiting Football Transfer Portal Video Watch on YouTube Listen on Apple Listen on Spotify Forum Members Login Heartland College Sports – An Independent Big 12 Today Blog | College Football News | Big 12 Today The Arizona Wildcats and Texas Tech Red Raiders meet on Saturday in Lubbock in a Top 25 showdown that could have major implications on the Big 12 Championship race. Both teams enter Week 9 at 6-1 overall and 3-1 in Big 12 play, but they're coming off completely different Saturdays. Arizona made another statement by crushing Iowa State 39-3, while Texas Tech suffered its first loss of the season in a 37-24 road defeat at Cincinnati. Now, Texas Tech returns home to a place where it has won 12 straight games, while Arizona gets another opportunity to prove it belongs among the top contenders in the Big 12. The matchup also features an intriguing battle between Noah Fifita and an aggressive Texas Tech defense that leads the country with five pick-sixes this season. Here is everything you need to know about Arizona vs. Texas Tech in Week 9, including our prediction and pick for Saturday's Big 12 showdown. Texas Tech vs. Arizona Odds Spread: Texas Tech -3.5 Over/Under: 54.5 Moneyline: Arizona +134/Texas Tech -160 Odds as of Tuesday afternoon. Odds are subject to change. The Biggest Question: Arizona's Passing Game vs. Texas Tech's Defense? The Red Raiders' defense has been underwhelming, at best. Texas Tech ranks 14th in the Big 12 Conference in passing yards allowed per game, ranking only ahead of Cincinnati and West Virginia. Now, this secondary does have 13 takeaways, which is tops in the Big 12. But that also tells me that they may be too aggressive , at times. And now they have to slow down Noah Fifita, who doesn't make many mistakes. He's thrown 18 touchdowns to just four interceptions this season and has the deepest wide receiver corps in the entire Big 12. Whoever wins this match up will win the game. Houston vs. Utah Prediction and Pick Prediction: Arizona 31, Texas Tech 24 Texas Tech was exposed last week at Cincinnati. Yes, they have talent, but they haven't been able to put it all together this season. And after Saturday, there's no evidence that it's magically going to happen against one of the most underrated teams in the country, Arizona, who is playing some of the best football in America right now. Since losing to BYU on the road (a game they led in the second half), Arizona has won five-straight games by an average of nearly 24 points. I haven't even talked about the other side of the ball, where Arizona is Top 5 in passing defense in yards allowed per game, and ranked 3rd in the Big 12 in yards allowed per carry (3.1). The front seven has been outstanding, as that impressive run defense has done it against the Top 2 rushing offenses in the league (West Virginia, Cincinnati). They've racked up 24 sacks in seven games, good for second in the Big 12, and now take on a Texas Tech offensive line that has been spotty, at best, throughout the season. Also, in a game that could come down to the final drive or two, Arizona's red zone defense ranks tops in the Big 12, while Texas Tech comes in at No. 14. And as the game wears on, the Tech defense could get worn down. Tech is second-to-last in the Big 12 in Time of Possession, while Arizona is in the Top 5, this despite having a pass-heavy offense. The icing on the cake on my pick? Special teams. Arizona is the best punt returning team in the Big 12. Texas Tech ranks 13th. These little things in a tough Top 25 match up can be the difference. And they will be come Saturday in Lubbock. And if you want to know where the sharp money is: 62% of the tickets are on Texas Tech, but over 80% of the money is on Arizona. The line opened up at Arizona +4.5 and is down to +3.5. If you can still get more than a field goal, jump on it. Arizona wins. Arizona covers. away.headline: Arizona football: CB Jay’Vion Cole to miss Texas Tech game, 2 injured receivers could return
away.blurb: CB Jay’Vion Cole is listed as out on the first availability report issued by the Big 12 Conference, one of four players ruled out for the matchup with the 13th-ranked Red Raiders.. Also out are tight end Shane King and defensive linemen Kevin Moore and Ezra Funa , the latter having not played yet this season. On the offensive side, receivers Chris Hunter and Giovanni Richardson are listed as questionable. Both have missed the past two games after getting hurt Oct. 3 vs. Cincinnati, the same game fellow WR Tre Spivey suffered a season-ending injury. Tight end Cole Rusk , who has been out several games, is listed as doubtful. Also listed as questionable are running back Ismail Mahdi and linebacker Max Harris but not because of injury. Both are seeking another emergency injunction to restore their eligibility after each appeared in a few games earlier this season. For Texas Tech, running back Cameron Dickey is listed as questionable. He’s missed the last two games with an ankle injury. Arizona could get back a pair of injured wide receivers for Saturday’s Top 25 showdown at Texas Tech, but it will also be without its lockdown corner Cole had started the first seven games this season, allowing only 16 catches on 30 targets, and is among the top-graded corners in the Big 12. In his absence the UA is likely to start Dwight Bootle II, who has been part of a 3-man rotation at the two corner spots with Cole and Tyrese Boss. Slot DB Malcolm Hartzog Jr. could also see time at corner.

away.headline: Texas Tech football's Cameron Dickey on track to return against Arizona
away.blurb: News Sports Autos Business Michigan Life + Home Entertainment Opinion Obituaries RED RAIDERS Texas Tech football's Cameron Dickey on track to return against Arizona Nathan Giese Lubbock Avalanche-Journal Updated Oct. 26, 2026, 2:06 p.m. ET Hear this story View Comments Coming off the team's first loss of the season, Joey McGuire said Texas Tech football could have a key offensive player back in the fold this week. The Texas Tech running back has been cleared to practice on Tuesday, where he'll go through scout and individual work, and should return to a full participant on Wednesday and will know more about Dickey's status later in the week. McGuire said Monday during his weekly press conference that the Red Raiders expect to have Cameron Dickey back on the field for this weekend's game against Arizona in Galaxy Stadium. "He should be good to go," McGuire said of Dickey. Dickey is second on the team in rushing, totaling 249 yards and four touchdowns on the season. He's missed the last two games after suffering a high ankle sprain in the win against Colorado. J'Koby Williams leads the team with 556 yards and five touchdowns on the ground. "I know he looked good last week," McGuire said, "and so it's going to be good to have him back. Just another guy that's been in some big games that's got a lot of experience and a lot of juice."

home.headline: Arizona football: CB Jay’Vion Cole to miss Texas Tech game, 2 injured receivers could return
home.blurb: CB Jay’Vion Cole is listed as out on the first availability report issued by the Big 12 Conference, one of four players ruled out for the matchup with the 13th-ranked Red Raiders.. Also out are tight end Shane King and defensive linemen Kevin Moore and Ezra Funa , the latter having not played yet this season. On the offensive side, receivers Chris Hunter and Giovanni Richardson are listed as questionable. Both have missed the past two games after getting hurt Oct. 3 vs. Cincinnati, the same game fellow WR Tre Spivey suffered a season-ending injury. Tight end Cole Rusk , who has been out several games, is listed as doubtful. Also listed as questionable are running back Ismail Mahdi and linebacker Max Harris but not because of injury. Both are seeking another emergency injunction to restore their eligibility after each appeared in a few games earlier this season. For Texas Tech, running back Cameron Dickey is listed as questionable. He’s missed the last two games with an ankle injury. Arizona could get back a pair of injured wide receivers for Saturday’s Top 25 showdown at Texas Tech, but it will also be without its lockdown corner Cole had started the first seven games this season, allowing only 16 catches on 30 targets, and is among the top-graded corners in the Big 12. In his absence the UA is likely to start Dwight Bootle II, who has been part of a 3-man rotation at the two corner spots with Cole and Tyrese Boss. Slot DB Malcolm Hartzog Jr. could also see time at corner.

home.headline: Texas Tech football's Cameron Dickey on track to return against Arizona
home.blurb: News Sports Autos Business Michigan Life + Home Entertainment Opinion Obituaries RED RAIDERS Texas Tech football's Cameron Dickey on track to return against Arizona Nathan Giese Lubbock Avalanche-Journal Updated Oct. 26, 2026, 2:06 p.m. ET Hear this story View Comments Coming off the team's first loss of the season, Joey McGuire said Texas Tech football could have a key offensive player back in the fold this week. The Texas Tech running back has been cleared to practice on Tuesday, where he'll go through scout and individual work, and should return to a full participant on Wednesday and will know more about Dickey's status later in the week. McGuire said Monday during his weekly press conference that the Red Raiders expect to have Cameron Dickey back on the field for this weekend's game against Arizona in Galaxy Stadium. "He should be good to go," McGuire said of Dickey. Dickey is second on the team in rushing, totaling 249 yards and four touchdowns on the season. He's missed the last two games after suffering a high ankle sprain in the win against Colorado. J'Koby Williams leads the team with 556 yards and five touchdowns on the ground. "I know he looked good last week," McGuire said, "and so it's going to be good to have him back. Just another guy that's been in some big games that's got a lot of experience and a lot of juice."

picks.headline: Iowa Hawkeyes football expert previews Week 9 showdown vs. Wisconsin
picks.blurb: Iowa Hawkeyes football expert previews Week 9 showdown vs. Wisconsin - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NCAAF College Fantasy Football College Football Playoff Packers defeat Panthers WNBA Finals: Dream force Game 7 Bears land DT Jeffery Simmons HS player bodychecks ref Red Wings suspend Larkin Iowa Hawkeyes football expert previews Week 9 showdown vs. Wisconsin Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads In roughly 24 hours, the Wisconsin Badgers will be playing at Kinnick Stadium for the 100th edition of the Battle for the Heartland Trophy. Iowa City, IA, plays host to this historic matchup , one that just so happens to take place on Halloween. For the first time since 2023, the Badgers are officially in the AP Top 25 . Remember, Iowa's shocking loss last Saturday to Minnesota knocked them out of the Top 25 entirely. Heading into this massive Big Ten showdown, Badgers Wire's Jordon Lawrenz had a chance to speak with Hawkeyes Wire's Josh Helmer . Iowa came into the year ranked No. 22, but just fell out of the AP Poll after a loss to Minnesota. Where have things gone wrong this season? Oct 24, 2026; Minneapolis, Minnesota, USA; Minnesota Golden Gophers players celebrate with the Floyd of Rosedale after beating the Iowa Hawkeyes at Huntington Bank Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Matt Krohn-Imagn Images There's questions at quarterback, which we can discuss in a moment. But, Iowa just hasn't run the football consistently enough. That adds extra pressure on its signal-callers, and it's been an ongoing issue against Power Four foes. Against the power conference teams on its schedule, Iowa has eclipsed the century mark on the ground just once. That was in the Hawkeyes' 41-24 road win at Washington, where Iowa ran for 263 yards. Losing someone to injury always hurts, but this is at least a team that has a ton of guys with 20+ carries on the year. How much of an impact does losing Kamari Moulton have on this offense? Iowa running back Kamari Moulton (28) celebrates 20-19 win over Michigan at Michigan Stadium in Ann Arbor on Saturday, Sept. 26, 2026. Unfortunately for Iowa, I think it could have a big impact. Kamari Moulton has been Iowa's clear No. 1 running back for a ground game that has struggled mightily at times against power foes. Moulton has been the lone bright spot. He was also the Hawkeyes' leading rusher a season ago. L.J. Phillips Jr., Braeden Jackson, and Xavier Williams are all serviceable, but it's going to be a drop off for Iowa until proven otherwise. The age old question is Hank Brown vs. Jeremy Hecklinski. Why do you think Kirk Ferentz keeps sticking with Brown? Oct 24, 2026; Minneapolis, Minnesota, USA; Iowa Hawkeyes quarterback Jeremy Hecklinski (10) and Iowa Hawkeyes quarterback Hank Brown (9) take the field before the game against the Minnesota Golden Gophers at Huntington Bank Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Matt Krohn-Imagn Images Ferentz pointed to the intricacies of the offense this week when asked if they were happy with how they operated after making the move to replace Jeremy Hecklinski with Hank Brown at Minnesota. It's not a shocking response. That's some of what we heard during fall camp. The ceiling is greater in the passing game with Hecklinski, but it sounds like he's been mistake-prone at times, too. Ultimately, I think Iowa feels that Brown is less mistake-prone and maybe operates the intricacies of Iowa's offense on a more consistent basis as compared to Hecklinski. Maddening for Hawkeye fans to try to figure out, though. Wisconsin's defense just held UCLA and USC to 24 combined points. Do you think Iowa can shake off a brutal 10-point showing at Minnesota now that the Hawkeyes are back at home on Halloween? Wisconsin linebacker Mason Posa (8) celebrates his fourth down tackle during the third quarter of their game against Michigan State Saturday, October 3, 2026 at Camp Randall Stadium in Madison, Wisconsin. I do. Ferentz typically gets a good response out of his teams following lackluster performances. This is a winnable game for Iowa, and the Hawkeyes are returning home to Kinnick Stadium which obviously helps. Score prediction? Will the Heartland Trophy stay in Iowa City? Oct 14, 2023; Madison, Wisconsin, USA; General view of The Heartland Trophy during the game between the Iowa Hawkeyes and Wisconsin Badgers at Camp Randall Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Jeff Hanisch-USA TODAY Sports Iowa 17, Wisconsin 13. I expect this to be a field position game without a lot of offense. While recent meetings have seen Iowa win by multiple scores or in blowout fashion each of the past two seasons, I don't expect anything similar on Saturday. Wisconsin appears to be much-improved, which is a credit to the terrific year-over-year job that Luke Fickell has done. At the end of the day, I like Iowa to lean on its tried-and-true formula: great defense and special teams, and just enough offense in the right moments to retain the Heartland Trophy. home.headline: Iowa star RB ruled out for season ahead of Badgers showdown
home.blurb: Iowa star RB ruled out for season ahead of Badgers showdown - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NCAAF Iowa star RB ruled out for season ahead of Badgers showdown The No. 25 Wisconsin Badgers will look to turn the page in their rivalry with the Iowa Hawkeyes, as they've been flat-out beaten the last two years, while the losing streak has now extended to four. Things have changed, though, this season, as the Badgers are now in the AP Top 25 after a win over the USC Trojans at Camp Randall Stadium this past weekend. Iowa, on the other hand, fell out of the Top 25 from No. 15 after a loss to the Minnesota Gophers this weekend. The Hawkeyes are still favored heading into this one, but Iowa will be without star running back Kamari Moulton, head coach Kirk Ferentz announced. Moulton is out for the season with an upper-body injury. Now, it had been an up-and-down year for Moulton and the Hawkeyes offense, as he's been limited to under 60 yards and four yards per carry in four of the team's six games this year. In the other two against Northern Illinois and Washington, however, Moulton went for 183 yards and two touchdowns, and 208 yards and two touchdowns, respectively. (Photo by Jesse Beals/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images Rohan Chakravarthi Wed, October 28, 2026 at 10:33 PM UTC · 2 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads In the 2010s, Wisconsin had won seven of the eight matchups between the two sides. However, in this decade, Iowa has won five of the six rivalry games, and remain holders of the Heartland Trophy heading into this weekend. It was a rough one for the Badgers last year, as they lost 37-0 at home in a demoralizing defeat. The year before, Wisconsin lost 42-10. This season, Moulton had ran for 541 yards and four touchdowns on 6.3 yards per carry. He was averaging 90.2 yards per game prior to suffering the injury against Minnesota. Iowa will now lean on junior Xavier Williams, who has rushed for 187 yards and three touchdowns this season on 7.5 yards per carry. Much of that production came in Iowa's win over Northern Iowa, where Williams went for 151 yards and three scores on just six carries. Outside of that game, he's rushed for 36 yards on 19 attempts this season. Last year, when the two sides played, Iowa went for over 200 yards and four touchdowns on the ground. Moulton had 96 yards and a touchdown, while Williams had 55 yards and two touchdowns in the 37-0 win. It's two different teams this year, but Saturday morning should be a competitive and physical battle nonetheless.

picks.blurb: ESPN predicts the winner of Saturday's game between Auburn and Ole Miss - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NCAAF College Fantasy Football College Football Playoff Packers defeat Panthers WNBA Finals: Dream force Game 7 Bears land DT Jeffery Simmons HS player bodychecks ref Red Wings suspend Larkin ESPN predicts the winner of Saturday's game between Auburn and Ole Miss Phillip Jordan, Auburn Wire Thu, October 29, 2026 at 7:00 PM UTC · 2 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The Auburn Tigers are looking to rebound after playing poorly in a 38-17 home loss to LSU. Who does ESPN have winning when Auburn travels to Ole Miss on Saturday? According to the ESPN Matchup Predictor , Auburn has a 25.1% chance of picking up a victory at Ole Miss. The Tigers have not lost back-to-back games this season and will be looking to avoid that in Oxford, Mississippi, on Saturday. It will be a tall task for Auburn to come away with a win over the Rebels, who are coming off a narrow defeat last week at the hands of the Texas Longhorns . Ole Miss almost made a huge comeback after trailing Texas 24-3 at halftime. Rebels quarterback Trinidad Chambliss could not find the end zone as time expired, and Ole Miss lost 34-27. At 5-2, Ole Miss can not afford another loss if they want to make the College Football Playoff. This will be the first meeting between the two schools since the 2023 season , when Ole Miss defeated Auburn in the first year of the Hugh Freeze era. These two programs met each year when they were both part of the SEC West division. Auburn leads the all-time series 35-12, but Ole Miss has won the last two meetings. In the final five games of the season, Auburn should be able to snap their streak of five consecutive losing seasons. With four wins, Auburn should be able to get three more victories with games against Arkansas, Mississippi State, and Samford. A matchup that could help Auburn pull off an upset victory over Ole Miss is in the run game. The Rebels are at the bottom of the SEC, giving up 161.1 yards per game on the ground. Saturday could be an opportunity for Byrum Brown and the Auburn running backs to have a big game. By Parker Gillam Published: Oct 27, 2026 · 8:56 PM EDT The grind of the 9-game SEC schedule has taken its toll on every team in the league, and nobody knows that better than Auburn and Ole Miss . Both the Tigers and Rebels have enjoyed incredible highs and head-scratching lows this season, with the former having upset Georgia then blown out by LSU the next week while the latter has gone from taking down those same Bayou Bengals to getting trampled by Florida, then returning the favor to Missouri before falling in Austin last weekend. All of that is to say that when Auburn and Ole Miss square off Saturday, each will be desperate for a victory. ESPN's Bill Connelly's SP+ cares not about desperation, instead trusting a series of metrics and simulations to predict games each week. And regarding the clash in Oxford, SP+ believes that the Rebels should be able to bounce back with a 32-21 win over the visiting Tigers, keeping their College Football Playoff hopes intact for just a bit longer ahead of some tough matchups down the stretch. picks.blurb: Auburn lost to No. 17 LSU, 38-17, last Saturday in Jordan-Hare Stadium. LSU dominated Auburn, outgaining them, 522-271. LSU quarterback Sam Leavitt scored four touchdowns. Auburn quarterback Byrum Brown was sacked seven times, and the Tigers' defense failed to create a turnover. Ole Miss is also coming off a loss. The Rebels fell to No. 11 Texas in Austin, 34-27. Ole Miss quarterback Trinidad Chambliss passed for 250 yards in the loss, but was picked off three times. Texas outgained Ole Miss 419-363 in total yards and 207-113 in rushing yards. Saturday's game will be the first between the Tigers and Rebels since the 2023 season, and the 49th meeting all-time. Auburn leads the series, 35-13. Ole Miss football is back in the Vaught after a grueling road loss to Texas. Pete Golding and company are looking to rebound against Auburn, and with playoff dreams on the line, the Rebels will need to put their best foot forward to keep them alive on Halloween. Here are our staff's Ole Miss vs. Auburn predictions, including score picks, X-factors and our boldest calls for Saturday. Ole Miss vs. Auburn predictions at a glance All nine of our writers are picking the Rebels. The average score prediction is Ole Miss 34, Auburn 21, and Makhi Frazier is the most popular X-factor pick with four votes as Ole Miss plays without Kewan Lacy. Score prediction Parks Burcham Ole Miss 35, Auburn 28 Makhi Frazier Luke Dunavant Ole Miss 27, Auburn 24 Ole Miss 34, Auburn 17 Ole Miss 38, Auburn 27 Stopping the QB run Ole Miss 28, Auburn 10 Trinidad Chambliss Jacob Quaglino Ole Miss 41, Auburn 17 Ole Miss 35, Auburn 21 Deuce Alexander Evie Van Pelt Ole Miss 34, Auburn 20 Staff Predictions Score Prediction: Ole Miss 35, Auburn 28 I know, I know. Just hear me out. Auburn quarterback Byrum Brown is one of the SEC's top rushers and will pose a threat to this Ole Miss defense. The Rebels held strong against Missouri but didn't hold as well against Texas in the run game. They need to contain Brown and make him a quarterback. I still have the Rebels. Trinidad Chambliss needs a rebound game, and this is the weekend for it. X-Factor: Makhi Frazier Makhi Frazier has been the No. 2 option in the running back room and has posed a threat to defenders. Now it is a little different with Kewan Lacy out for what might be an extended period. Frazier needs to show everyone what he can do. Bold Prediction: Trinidad Chambliss rebounds strongly and reminds the world what kind of quarterback he is Score Prediction: Ole Miss 27, Auburn 24 I'm back on the light side, I guess. Ole Miss is very good at home, so I think they will be able to squeak a win out against a pretty good Auburn team. Also, 13.5 is way too many points. X-Factor: Run Defense This is the x-factor the rest of the way. Byrum Brown is a very good runner, and if he gets going, it's going to be ugly. You have to make Auburn beat you through the air, which Ole Miss will be able to take advantage of. Bold Prediction: Byrum Brown rushes for 100+ in a losing effort Score Prediction: Ole Miss 34, Auburn 17 With the confirmed absence of Kewan Lacy, Frazier needs to continue his recent success, but this time it is up to him to establish the rushing attack. I believe if he can get going, this offense will be able to go up and down the field all day. Bold Prediction: Ole Miss gets 2 turnovers Byrum Brown is very talented; however, he has struggled with ball security, throwing 7 interceptions and just 8 touchdowns. In addition, Ole Miss' defense has found something lately, forcing a turnover in each game since their bye week. Score Prediction: Ole Miss 38, Auburn 27 The Ole Miss Rebels are looking to regain some momentum as they come back home to battle Auburn this week, and I firmly believe that they will. This game will be a high-scoring showdown, and I just don't think that Byrum Brown and the Tiger offense will be able to keep up, but it all depends on whether the Rebel defense will be able to make timely stops. X-Factor: Stopping the Quarterback Run One thing the Rebs have often struggled with this season is stopping the run. This is something that I believe they will be determined to do as they face the elusive Brown and the Tigers' ground attack. The game will come down to defenders staying disciplined and making tackles. Bold Prediction: Makhi Frazier Breakout Game My bold prediction for this week is that Makhi Frazier will rush for at least 120 yards. With the absence of Kewan Lacy , he will be looking to prove that he can be the number one running back, which will open up the offense and allow for the play-action game to be even more unstoppable. Score Prediction: Ole Miss 28, Auburn 10 Ole Miss returns home to host the Auburn Tigers as they get set for the final five games of the regular season. The Rebels are coming off a heartbreaking 34-27 loss to Texas on the road. X-Factor: Trinidad Chambliss Chambliss throws for 175 yards with two touchdowns and one with his legs. Bold Prediction: The defense returns strong this weekend and puts up numbers as they did against Missouri, making it hard for Auburn to move the ball. Score Prediction: Ole Miss 41, Auburn 17 With the Rebels heading back to Oxford after a rip-your-heart-out loss in Austin, the time is now for Chambliss and co. to bounce back and play their best football, with the margin for error now likely gone. An Auburn team that hasn't exactly impressed when it comes to pass defense especially lays the groundwork for arguably the nation's best QB to have a career day in front of a home crowd, where he rarely hasn't performed well. The team's ability to play on the road remains a concern for sure, but for this week, there is little reason to believe the Rebels won't keep their playoff hopes alive playing at Vaught-Hemingway, with one of the nation's top QBs and a struggling Auburn pass defense. If Chambliss has a day we know he's capable of having, and that's what the indications are, it's going to be really tough to envision an Auburn victory. Bold Prediction: Chambliss throws for five touchdowns and 400 or more yards As mentioned before, the Rebels, and Trinidad Chambliss, are known to put up video game numbers at home. And while nothing can ever be taken for granted (Auburn did win in Athens, after all), Rebel fans know they have a QB with the poise and maturity to avoid complacency, something that will become even clearer with the margin for error now likely eliminated. Knowing that every game is a playoff game at this point will ensure that the Grand Rapids, Mich., native will be nothing short of determined to play to his maximum potential, and against a struggling Auburn pass defense, that could mean career-defining numbers. Score Prediction: Ole Miss 38, Auburn 27 Pete Golding and Ole Miss return home where they’ve become practically unstoppable over the last two seasons. They’ll face an Auburn team that recently got pummeled by LSU after a shocking win over Georgia the week before. I predict the Rebs will get back on track this week, winning 38-27. My X-Factor is Makhi Frazier, who will need to establish a strong ground presence with Kewan Lacy injured. Bold Prediction: Trinidad Returns to Normal As far as bold predictions, I’m confident Trinidad will get back on track this week. I believe the veteran QB won’t throw any interceptions and will combine for over 3.5 total touchdowns. Score Prediction: Ole Miss 35, Auburn 21 X-Factor: Deuce Alexander I look for Deuce to rack up close to 100 yards receiving and two scores against Auburn’s secondary. Bold Prediction: Trinidad Chambliss runs for 25+ yards. Score Prediction: Ole Miss 34, Auburn 20 Back home, where they’ve won 15 straight, the Rebels bounce back from Austin. Auburn’s Byrum Brown will make some plays with his legs, but Ole Miss has too much offense, averaging 36 points a game, and the Vaught-Hemingway crowd will make it tough on the Tigers at 11:45 in the morning. It’s closer than the score at halftime, but Ole Miss pulls away in the fourth quarter. X-Factor: RB Makhi Frazier With Kewan Lacy out, this is Frazier’s backfield. He ran for 101 yards against Missouri, the last time Ole Miss played at home, and had a 34-yard run at Texas. If he can give the Rebels a steady run game early, it takes pressure off Trinidad Chambliss and keeps Brown on the sideline. Look for Frazier to top 100 yards again and find the end zone. Bold Prediction: Ole Miss scores a touchdown on its opening drive Outside of Charlotte, the Rebels haven’t scored on an opening possession all season, gaining minus-2 yards on those six drives combined. That changes Saturday. Golding has spent the week looking at everything from the coin toss to the early play calls, and Ole Miss marches down the field to open the game, with Chambliss running it in himself. Golding did say we’d see a little more of him running. Ole Miss will face the Auburn Tigers in Vaught-Hemingway Stadium this Saturday. Kickoff is set for 11:45 a.m. CT, and the game will be broadcast on SEC Network. Until then, follow along with The Rebel Walk for the best coverage. home.headline: Another SEC game, another crowded Ole Miss injury report
home.blurb: One of the biggest storylines to watch before kickoff Saturday won't involve Auburn at all. It'll be who Ole Miss has available. The Rebels could be without several key contributors when they host Auburn, with offensive tackle Terez Davis and cornerback Jalyn Crawford listed as questionable. Safety Edwin Joseph and running back Kewan Lacy have already been ruled out. Those are two big losses, but not unexpected ones . Davis is the biggest name to monitor. The veteran offensive tackle missed last week's loss to Texas, and his status remains uncertain heading into the weekend. If he's unable to play, Ole Miss will once again have to adjust along an offensive line that has spent much of the season searching for consistency and continuity. That could become even more complicated if Brycen Sanders or Connor Howes see their statuses downgraded from probable. The secondary also enters the game with some uncertainty. Crawford's availability is still in question, while Joseph continues working his way back from ankle surgery. The veteran safety has been rehabbing daily, but his recovery has taken longer than the Rebels initially hoped, keeping one of their most experienced defensive backs off the field. Lacy will also miss Saturday's matchup as he continues recovering from a shoulder injury. His absence will put a larger workload on the rest of Ole Miss' running back room as the Rebels look to establish more balance offensively against an Auburn team that has been one of the SEC's most unpredictable groups this season. picks.headline: Odds Have Changed for Georgia Football vs. Florida Gators
picks.blurb: Odds Have Changed for Georgia Football vs. Florida Gators Skip to main content SI.COM SI.COM BULLDOGS FB SI.COM BULLDOGS BB FOOTBALL FOOTBALL NEWS BASKETBALL NEWS ATHENS - Odds have been updated to Georgia Football’s massive clash with the Florida Gators 48 hours before the rivals face off in Atlanta. The Bulldogs and Gators are playing a one-off game in Atlanta this season , and one next year in Tampa as Jacksonville (the traditional home for this game) rebuilds its stadium. The anticipation for the game is growing as the weekend grows near. What’s also growing is the betting line for the game. On Sunday FanDuel listed the Bulldogs as a 9.5-point favorite over the Gators. DraftKings had UGA as a 10.5-point favorite in the contest. Both betting houses now have Georgia as a 12.5-point favorite to win the game. The move in the line is a fairly significant one - placing the game firmly into double-digit territory. Of course, betting lines are only an indication of what experts feel is expected to happen - they are not a guarantee of an outcome. There are two reasons the line has be crept up over the week. First, both of Florida’s quarterbacks are injured in some form. Athens-area native Aaron Philo started the first six games of the Gators’ season, but missed Florida’s 27-24 win at Texas with a shoulder injury. Tramell Jones started for the Gators in that game and guided the Gators to an upset in Austin. Jones has “wear-and-tear” injuries. Georgia football TE Jaden Reddell celebrates with Georgia football RB Chauncey Bowens after scoring a touchdown against Vanderbilt. | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Florida coach Jon Sumrall said Monday that he would not name a starter at that time. Florida coach Jon Sumrall said Monday that he would not name a starter at that time. “Both guys are available - believe in both guys,” Sumrall told reporters. “Not going to name a starter today. We need both those guys to be ready to play.” Both Gator quarterbacks were listed as questionable Wednesday night on the SEC’s mandated injury report. In addition, Georgia got very good news with an upgrade for running back Chauncey Bowens, who was upgraded to questionable from out, which is where he’s been the last few weeks. Bowens scored the game-winning touchdown against the Gators last year in Jacksonville. Second, there was likely some overreaction to Georgia’s upset loss to Auburn at home, and the Gators’ upset win on the road at Florida. Most of the summer this game was listed around the 12-point mark. Florida’s play early in the season dropped the number under ten points, but that recovered to back over double digits after Florida was blown out in back-to-back losses to Missouri and South Carolina. But only twice in modern history has a double-digit favorite lost this game (1997 and 2014). In both upsets turnovers and a robust run game powered the underdog to an unexpected win. Since 2010, the Bulldogs have been favored to beat the Gators 13 times in the last 16 games. Georgia is 11-5 straight up against the Gators since then - losing in overtime as a one-point favorite in 2010, a 10-point favorite in 2014, a 3-point underdog in 2015, a 6.5-point underdog in 2016 and a 3-point favorite in 2020. On average the Dawgs have been a 6.5-point favorite to beat Florida since 2010. The team that runs the ball better in the World’s Largest Outdoor Cocktail Party is 15-1 since 2010 (2020 - Florida, 44-28). Odds refresh periodically and are subject to change. picks.blurb: Three Bold Prediction's for Georgia Football's Showdown with Florida in Atlanta Skip to main content SI.COM SI.COM BULLDOGS FB SI.COM BULLDOGS BB FOOTBALL FOOTBALL NEWS BASKETBALL NEWS The Georgia Bulldogs will face off against the Florida Gators in the World’s Largest Outdoor Cocktail Party , except this time it may take place indoors. While EverBank Stadium in Jacksonville undergoes renovation, the game is taking a two game hiatus from Duval County. The game will take place in Mercedes-Benz stadium in Atlanta on Saturday. Depending on the weather, the roof could be closed, hence the party being inside. This will be a very different atmosphere for this historic rivalry. Now, Florida fans will see that Jacksonville is not that neutral of a site. Atlanta is the equivalent in Georgia. So, that means some ridiculous things could happen Saturday afternoon. Here are three bold predictions for Saturday: Gunner Stockton Totals 4 Touchdowns Gunner Stockton is coming off of the worst game of his life, where he turned the ball over three times for the first time in his career, including the untimely fumble at the end of the game. That fumble led to Auburn’s game-winning field goal. Florida has the second worst passing defense in the SEC. Stockton is one of the best and most efficient quarterbacks in the nation. A bounce back game seems likely, and he will total at least four scores. Georgia Wins Turnover Margin by 2 The Dawgs lost the turnover battle to Auburn 0-3, and they almost won. Georgia has been better about creating turnover opportunities this year than it was last season. Georgia has also had a knack for winning games despite losing the turnover battle. This game last year is an example of that. Georgia is due for a big turnover game. The Dawgs only have two takeaways over the last three games. Jadan Baugh Gets His Jadan Baugh is arguably college football’s best running back. He has simmered down since his 600-yard and 11-touchdown start over the first four games. Rushing for over 90 yards and a score en route to an upset road win over Texas can be considered a bounce back. Georgia’s run defense has progressively gotten worse as the season has gone on. Alabama was able to rip off some expl;osive and total about 160 yards on the ground. Byrum Brown ran all over the Dawgs, helping Auburn total over 190 rushing yards. Baugh is good enough to get his. Georgia is good enough to win even if that happens. I think he will have around 100 total yards and a score. For the first time in the history of the World's Largest Outdoor Cocktail Party, Florida and Georgia will play in Atlanta at Mercedes-Benz Stadium, with kickoff slated for Saturday at 3:30 p.m. ET (ABC). The Bulldogs are 11.5-point favorites, and my Florida vs. Georgia prediction and college football picks expect Kirby Smart's team to take advantage of Jon Sumrall's defense in his first Cocktail Party. Who will win Florida vs Georgia: Georgia -11.5 Kirby Smart has owned the Florida vs. Georgia rivalry recently, winning eight of the last nine games. While he's just 5-4 against the spread in those games, his Bulldogs have the advantage against a sporadic Florida team. But without knowing which version of Florida we'll get, I would only take the Bulldogs up to -12.5 . Georgia's defense is far more trustworthy than Florida's, ranking 14th nationally in available yards percentage (35.7%) , 21st in defensive success rate (35.4%), and holding six of seven opponents to 20 or fewer points. With athletes like Chris Cole and Ellis Robinson IV, Georgia is well-equipped to deal with Buster Faulkner's misdirection-heavy offense. Plus, the Gators' top two QBs ( Aaron Philo , Tramell Jones Jr. ) are questionable , and while I expect them to play, it could impact their consistency. In a high-scoring game, Georgia's defense will make enough stops to cover. TOP PICK Florida vs Georgia Over/Under pick: Over 54.5 Georgia has been an Over machine this season, hitting it in six of seven games, despite its defense allowing just 15.9 points per game. I like the Over to hit at 55.5 or better for the fifth time in the last seven Cocktail Parties, especially given Faulkner's familiarity with Smart and Georgia's defense. Faulkner worked for Smart at Georgia for three years before spending the last three seasons as Georgia Tech's offensive coordinator; his offenses averaged 24.6 points and 392 yards against the Bulldogs. With one of the top running backs in the country in Jadan Baugh , who ranks top 10 in forced missed tackles (40), Florida should score 20+. Its defense will do the rest of the job for the Over. Florida has one of the worst defenses in the Power Four, r anking 125th in the country in defensive success rate (49.5%) , and it hasn't played an offense as efficient as Georgia's yet this season. Florida vs Georgia combo Some weeks Florida looks like a College Football Playoff team (against Ole Miss and Texas ), and other weeks it looks like it might not win eight games (against Missouri and South Carolina ). Which version will come to play in the World's Largest Cocktail Party? If Auburn hadn't improbably upset the Bulldogs the last time they played, they would probably be closer to 14.5-point favorites because of Florida's defensive struggles and offensive injuries. Coming out of a bye, I expect Smart to have Georgia ready to roll in a rivalry game he's dominated and to pull away in the second half against a Florida defense that ranks second-worst in havoc rate in the SEC (14.5%). This time the Bulldogs are listed as a 10.5-point favorite to topple the Gators in Atlanta on Halloween according to Draft Kings . It is another in a string of games where the Bulldogs have been favorites to beat their biggest SEC rival. Georgia has not been an underdog against the Gators since 2016 - the first year Kirby Smart took over as the head coach in Athens. Should the line remain unchanged at kickoff it would be the sixth time since that year that Georgia has been a double-digit favorite to win the game. Georgia's 24-20 win over Gators in Jacksonville last fall was the first time UGA had been favored by fewer than ten points in five seasons. One of the keys to success for Kirby Smart's program over his tenure in Athens has been the Dawgs' ability to slow or even stop the Gators running the ball effectively. Georgia football RB Nate Frazier (3) pushes off Florida Gators defensive back Cormani McClain. | USA TODAY Network via Reuters Connect Florida has not eclipsed the 120-yard mark on the ground since going for 161 in a 34-7 loss to the Dawg in 2021. Florida has been up and down running the ball this season - even with one of the best running backs in the nation... Jadan Baugh. Baugh has been solid against the Dawgs - going for 136 yards on 32 carries with a touchdown. With the Gators' quarterback situation in flux, Baugh might be the singularly-important player in the game. South Carolina and Missouri slowed the Atlanta native in their two wins against the Gators. But against Texas, Baugh was a workhorse again - scoring once on the ground after carrying the ball 25 times for 91 yards. Baugh blistered Auburn (162 yards; 3 TDs) and Ole Miss (142 yards; 3 TDs) earlier this season. Georgia is 7-4 all time when allowing a 100-yard rusher under Kirby Smart. Georgia had a tremendous start to the season defending the run, but has had back-to-back games on run defense that are as bad as they have had dating back to the end of the 2024 season. The Bulldogs have only covered once in the last four games against the Gators - in 2023 thanks to a late-game touchdown from Dwight Phillips. This is the first time since 2018 that UGA is coming off a loss going into a scheduled bye week. The Dawgs are 17-3 all time after losses and 12-3 after a bye under Kirby Smart. The Dawgs and Gators meet in Mercedes-Benz Stadium in Atlanta for the first time ever. The game, which is traditionally held in Jacksonville, is on a two-year hiatus from there so that massive renovations can take place to upgrade the facility there. Georgia has played in Mercedes-Benz Stadium each year it has been open. Odds refresh periodically and are subject to change. The Georgia-Florida game will be televised on ABC. Georgia is favored by almost two touchdowns against Florida . Both teams are coming off bye weeks and are looking to stay in the College Football Playoff and SEC championship hunt. The Bulldogs have won five straight games in the series, but looked far from invincible in their 27-24 home loss to the Auburn Tigers before their bye week. With stadium renovations taking place in Jacksonville , the rivalry will be played in Atlanta this year. Both teams enter the game ranked for the first time since 2020, which is also the last time the Gators won it. UF (5-2, 3-2 in SEC) comes in hot after its second win over a top-10 team this season, a 27-24 victory at Texas . Backup quarterback Tramell Jones Jr. impressed with two touchdown passes and the game-sealing run, raising questions over whether he or Aaron Philo will get the start this week. Georgia (6-1, 4-1) fell from the ranks of the unbeaten two weeks ago when Byrum Brown spurred a late drive that led to Auburn's unbelievable 27-24 in Athens. Gunner Stockton threw for 272 yards and two score but also tossed a pair of interceptions, the second straight game in which he matched his TD and INT numbers. Buy Florida vs. Georgia football tickets Here's when the Gators and Bulldogs square off this week. Florida football schedule: UF's next game What time is UF vs UGA? The Gators and Bulldogs kick off at 3:30 p.m. on Saturday at Mercedes-Benz Stadium in Atlanta. Florida vs Georgia prediction The Bulldogs have looked like the best team in the SEC all year and have numbers to show it: They rank first in the conference in both scoring offense (43 points per game) and defense (15.9 ppg). The obvious mismatch in this game comes through the air. UGA has a top-30 passing offense that has eight players with at least 100 yards receiving. UF fields a bottom-20 pass defense that allowed two straight embarrassing losses before the big Texas win. Florida has been able to counteract its deficiencies by getting to the quarterback, tying Georgia for third in the SEC with 22 sacks. UGA has protected Stockton well, though, allowing just eight sacks all year. The Gators' other big strength — Jadan Baugh and their 30th-ranked rushing attack — can also be undone by the Dawgs with their No. 10 run defense. Then again, Auburn did just run for 192 yards on them a week after Alabama put up 161 on them. This projects as Florida's best chance in years to unseat their rivals, but this being an unofficial road game might prove to be the difference. away.blurb: As it turns out, a major reason for their dip in performance -- one of their star wide receivers being out -- appears set to resolve itself this week as Vernell Brown returns to the field. Brown was listed as probable on the team's injury report this week, and it looks like he is going to come back and be a huge piece of this Gators offense against the Bulldogs on Saturday afternoon. Now, going up against Georgia, Brown makes his grand return after it's obvious the offense the last three games did not look the same without him as it did in the beginning of the season. On paper, the Bulldogs have the unit to stifle the Gators offense, but if Brown's return makes them a whole lot closer to the version the SEC saw over the first month of the season than the second one, Georgia could wind up being in some trouble here. In order to continue their winning streak against the Gators, the Dawgs are going to have to handle a new version of the program this week led by a new head coach in Jon Sumrall. While Florida may not be quite the national title contender they looked like at the beginning of the season, they have proven capable of beating some great teams, and Georgia must be ready. Through the first four games of the year, Brown had 17 catches for 271 yards and two touchdowns and was a huge part of the Florida offense being so difficult for opposing teams to stop. As a freshman in 2025, Brown had more than 500 yards on the year despite playing in a dysfunctional offense, and he was looking to take a huge step this year. It's a great rivalry game though, and seeing both teams at full strength should be what everyone wants in order to have the best game possible. The SEC and college football in general are better when Florida and the Dawgs are battling at a high level, and it looks like that could be the case this weekend. Even though it will look a bit different in Atlanta, fans should be treated to a good one in this indoor version of the rivalry.

away.headline: Gators Injury Report: Both Quarterbacks Listed Ahead of Georgia Game
away.blurb: The most glaring of the ailments listed Wednesday evening are those that Florida’s quarterbacks suffer from heading into Saturday. Aaron Philo and Tramell Jones Jr. both made their way onto the list, with each’s status deemed as questionable heading into the Invesco QQQ Atlanta Gridiron Classic. Philo is named on the availability report for the second straight game week following a shoulder injury late in the loss to South Carolina. That same injury kept the Georgia Tech transfer out of Florida’s last game against Texas and puts his status in question against a team he carries a specific distaste for. “Both guys are available. I believe in both guys,” Sumrall said Monday. “I’m not going to name a starter today. We need both guys ready to play.” UF’s skill players are also dealing with their wealth of injuries, as wide receiver Bailey Stockton is doubtful following his momentary exit against Texas due to an ankle injury. Running back Duke Clark is also on the list as questionable and continues to nurse an injury against South Carolina that stationed him on the sidelines in a walking boot. Along with them, Vernell Brown III is probable and graces the injury list for the fourth straight week following his knee strain in the win against Ole Miss. While the Gators’ leading receiver is uncertain, Sumrall had optimistic thoughts on Brown’s availability for Saturday. The good injury news stops there for UF, with a key defensive player deemed out already. EDGE Jaden Robinson may miss his first game of the season with an undisclosed injury after logging 25 tackles and one sack across his first seven appearances in 2026. Georgia has already ruled three players out, as well as three players questionable for the first ranked matchup in the rivalry since 2020. Despite the injuries, the UGA enters as a 10.5-point favorite on most sportsbooks. away.headline: Florida football injury update | Two QBs listed as questionable for Georgia
away.blurb: News Sports Opinion Guardian Real Estate Advertise Obituaries eNewspaper Legals FOOTBALL Florida football injury update | Two QBs listed as questionable for Georgia Kevin Brockway Gainesville Sun Updated Oct. 28, 2026, 8:56 p.m. ET Florida football made its quarterback situation even more cloudy heading into its matchup against rival Georgia in Atlanta. The top two Florida Gators quarterbacks on the depth chart − Aaron Philio and Tramell Jones Jr.−are both listed as questionable for UF's showdown with the Bulldogs. Philo, who started UF's first six games for the Gators , sat out Florida 's game against Texas on October 17 with a shoulder injury. Jones, who led UF to an upset win over the Longhorns by passing for 155 yards and 2 TDs, is dealing with an undisclosed injury. "He’s got a couple of bumps and bruises, too, now," Sumrall said. "And he had, you know, pulled the guy fresh out of that garage and he goes and plays, and he got a couple fender-benders. So, there's some bumps and bruises he's dealing with that are new. I noticed it last week." Also on the availability report, inside linebacker Jaden Robinson and wide receiver Bailey Stockton are listed as doubtful for UF, while running back Duke Clark has been upgraded to questionable. Wide receiver Vernell Brown III, who has missed UF's last three games with a knee strain, is listed as probable. For Georgia, wide receiver Thomas Blackshear, outside linebacker Amaris Williams and safety Tyriq Green have been ruled out. Preseason All-SEC safety KJ Bolden is listed as questionable, along with running back Chauncey Bowens and wide receiver Isiah Canon. Florida coach Jon Sumrall said both practiced this week and hinted Jones was dealing with issues following the Texas win during his opening week press conference on October 26. If Jones and Philo both can't go, Florida would turn to its third-string quarterback, redshirt junior Aidan Warner, or true freshman Will Griffin. Warner appeared in the Florida-Georgia game in 2024 when DJ Lagway went down with a hamstring injury and made one career start the following week at Texas. No. 20 Florida (5-2. 3-2 SEC) is looking to break five-game losing streak against the Bulldogs (6-1, 4-1 SEC) when the two schools meet on Saturday, October 31 (3:30 p.m., ABC). The game, traditionally held in Jacksonville, was moved to Mercedes-Benz Stadium in Atlanta due to the $1.4 billion renovation at EverBank Stadium for the NFL's Jacksonville Jaguars. Kevin Brockway is The Gainesville Sun’s Florida beat writer. Contact him at kbrockway@gannett.com. Follow him on X @KevinBrockwayG1.

picks.headline: Previewing Northwestern's Upcoming Matchup Against Oregon as They Prepare to Face Another Tough Test on the Road
picks.blurb: Previewing Northwestern's Upcoming Matchup Against Oregon as They Prepare to Face Another Tough Test on the Road Skip to main content SI.COM Olympic Sports More from Northwestern Wildcats On SI FOOTBALL The Wildcats hit the road once again, this time traveling west to Eugene, Oregon, for a Big Ten showdown against the Oregon Ducks on Saturday at 2:30 p.m. CT. Oregon enters Saturday’s matchup looking to bounce back following a 21-10 loss to Illinois. The Ducks have been without starting quarterback Dante Moore for the past three games, and recent reports indicate he is unlikely to return this season after suffering a concussion earlier this year against USC. Oregon now sits at 10th in the conference with a 4-3 overall record this season. Meanwhile, the Wildcats enter Saturday’s matchup fresh off a commanding 42-14 home victory over Rutgers, a win that propelled Northwestern to No. 20 in the AP Poll. A familiar face will return to Eugene this weekend, as former Oregon head coach Chip Kelly will take on the Ducks, this time as the Wildcats’ offensive coordinator. Under Kelly’s leadership, Northwestern’s offense has emerged as one of the best in the Big Ten this season, ranking third in the conference in total yards and points per game and second in rushing yards per game. The Wildcats head to Eugene looking to build on their success on both sides of the ball and extend their four-game winning streak. A major contributor to Northwestern’s offensive success this season has been quarterback Aidan Chiles, this week’s Big Ten Offensive Player of the Week, who has thrown for over 1,600 yards and 12 touchdowns, while recording just one interception. Chiles was dominant last time out against Rutgers, throwing for 219 yards and passing for three touchdowns, while rushing for 83 yards and two touchdowns. Credit: David Banks- | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Alongside Chiles, wide receiver Griffin Wilde has been another standout for David Braun’s squad, recording 39 receptions for 615 yards and four touchdowns this season. Alongside Chiles, wide receiver Griffin Wilde has been another standout for David Braun’s squad, recording 39 receptions for 615 yards and four touchdowns this season. Northwestern’s rushing attack has also been a major part of its offensive success, led by the dynamic running back duo of Caleb Komolafe and Joseph Himon II, who have combined for over 900 rushing yards this season. Komolafe delivered an especially impressive performance against Rutgers, rushing for 150 yards and a touchdown in the Wildcats’ convincing victory. Defensively, Northwestern has remained stout this season, spearheaded by defensive back Robert Fitzgerald and line backer Braydon Brus. Despite missing the last two games due to injury, Fitzgerald has recorded 49 tackles and two interceptions this season. The defensive back leads the Big Ten in tackles per game with nine, followed closely by Brus in second with 8.9. Brus leads the defensive unit with 62 tackles and has also notched an interception and fumble recovery this season. Despite Dante Moore’s potential absence the rest of the season, Northwestern will still face a tough challenge on the road against a talented Oregon team. Quarterbacks Dylan Raiola and Brock Thomas have shared playing time the past three games for the Ducks. Raiola struggled in last weekend’s loss to Illinois, completing 27 of 41 passes for 246 yards, as the defeat dealt a major blow to Oregon’s hopes of reaching the College Football Playoff for a third consecutive season. Following the loss, Oregon made changes to its coaching staff, firing offensive coordinator Drew Mehringer. Mehringer had been promoted to the role at the start of the season after Will Stein departed to become the head coach at Kentucky, but his tenure was ultimately short-lived. This weekend’s matchup will be just the third time that both teams will be meeting, and the first time that they will match up at Autzen Stadium. They have split results, with Oregon taking the most recent matchup last season. Stay up to date on the Wildcats by bookmarking Northwestern On SI and follow us on Twitter.
