After entering the season ranked as high as they've ever been, the Ducks (4-3, 2-2 Big Ten) are unranked and out of the immediate College Football Playoff race after a stunning loss to Illinois on the road . The Ducks don't have much time to lick their wounds, either. After firing offensive coordinator Drew Mehringer and announcing quarterback Dante Moore will miss the rest of the 2026 season , one-loss Northwestern comes to town . Chip Kelly, who guided Oregon to a national championship game appearance as head coach over a decade ago, is the Wildcats' offensive coordinator. "It's almost like you're playing three different offenses," Oregon coach Dan Lanning said of Northwestern. "The new wrinkles that (Kelly) has at Northwestern, some of the old flavor that he has that he's carried all the way to his time back here at Oregon. There's always going to be something new when you walk into a game that it's going to be like he's never put this on film. He might not know how you're going to line up against it, and you have to figure it out there within the rules of your defense and how you execute." How it happened Oregon football, Dan Lanning react to lifeless loss vs. Illinois Oregon moves forward without its star QB and offensive coordinator Oregon vs. Northwestern scouting report Why Oregon has an advantage: The Ducks will have the home crowd behind them in Eugene and also have deep familiarity with Northwestern's starting quarterback, Aidan Chiles. The senior signal-caller started his career at Oregon State before transferring to Michigan State in 2024. Chiles played at Autzen Stadium in that year and had a rough outing, completely just 10 of 17 passes for 154 yards in a 31-10 loss. The Ducks found ways to rattle Chiles early, and with a strong pass rush in recent weeks they could do so again Saturday. Why Northwestern has an advantage: The Wildcats, under first-year offensive coordinator and former Ducks coach Chip Kelly, have one of the most efficient offenses in the country and don't make many mistakes. Northwestern isn't necessarily an offensive juggernaut, but it ranks fifth in the country in turnover margin and moves the ball methodically while keeping opposing teams out of the end zone defensively. Though the Wildcats' defense gives up plenty of yards, they rank in the top 25 in scoring defense allowing just 16.6 points per game. Oregon running back Jordon Davison, right, eludes Illinois defensive lineman Carter Janki and scores a touchdown during the first half at Gies Memorial Stadium in Champaign, Illinois on Oct. 24, 2026. Oregon vs. Northwestern injury updates Note: Official availability reports, mandated by the Big Ten, are released every day starting at 5 p.m. Wednesday leading up to kickoff. This story was published before the reports were made public. For Oregon: The Ducks will have a good chunk of playmakers returning to the sideline this weekend after sitting out last week due to unknown reasons. Evan Stewart, who was out last week after a DUII arrest, is expected back, as are Jalen Lott and Messiah Hampton. Lanning did not elaborate why Hampton and Lott missed last week. The coach also announced quarterback Dante Moore will likely miss the rest of the 2026 season after sustaining a concussion in late September. For Northwestern: The Wildcats were without several key contributors last week in a win against Rutgers, especially defensively. Second-leading tackler Robert Fitzgerald was held out, as well as defensive lineman Brendan Flakes. Oregon defensive back Peyton Woodyard, left, tries to catch the ball as it is deflected off Illinois wide receiver Collin Dixon during the second half at Gies Memorial Stadium in Champaign, Illinois on Oct. 24, 2026. Oregon vs. Northwestern: 4 bold predictions Ducks will mostly contain vaunted Northwestern run game Though Chiles has been successful through the air in recent weeks, Northwestern's bread and butter is establishing the ground game. After a subpar performance stopping the run last week against Illinois, Oregon's defense will show up ready to play and stifle backs Caleb Komolafe, Joseph Himon II and Gavin Sawchuk. Outside of games versus Oklahoma State and Illinois, Oregon's run defense has been sound and it'll look like a motivated group against a physical Wildcats team this weekend. Gage Hurych will have a bounce-back performance vs. Wildcats After missing three field goals last week in a loss to Illinois, all from 40 yards or more, junior kicker Gage Hurych will have a strong game against Northwestern. The Wildcats give up a lot of yards with a bend-but-don't-break defense but are elite in the red zone, an area where Oregon's offense struggles. Northwestern opponents only score a touchdown on 40% of possessions that reach the red zone. If Oregon's offense stalls as it gets closer to the end zone, look for Hurych to have a bounce-back performance with more manageable field-goal attempts. Ducks' defense will keep them in it until the end Though Oregon's offense will likely still have trouble after firing Drew Mehringer, its defense will respond and keep them in the game until the fourth quarter. Outside of a couple of broken off runs in a loss to Illinois, the Ducks' defense has been one of the top units in the country over the last month and that will continue against Northwestern this weekend. It just won't be enough to get a win, unless the offense really corrects itself. What will be the final result? The Oregon Ducks and Northwestern Wildcats enter Saturday’s matchup with very different expectations than they had at the beginning of the season. Oregon was expected to compete for a College Football Playoff spot, but a disappointing season, quarterback Dante Moore’s season-ending injury, and offensive coaching changes have left the Ducks searching for answers. Northwestern, meanwhile, has emerged as one of the biggest surprises in college football, entering the matchup at 6-1 and looking to strengthen its postseason resume. Can the Wildcats take advantage of Oregon’s struggles and leave Autzen Stadium with a statement victory? Or will the Ducks’ talent advantage be enough to get them back on track? Here is how the A to Z Sports team sees Saturday’s game playing out. A to Z Sports Score Predictions Tyler Forness — A to Z Sports Florida Prediction: Northwestern 24, Oregon 14 Going into the season, projecting the Wildcats to beat the Ducks would have been a shocker. On Halloween, it won’t be a trick, but rather a Wildcat treat. What Chip Kelly has done with this offense and head coach David Braun overall has been very impressive. They aren’t just 6-1 overall this season, but rank seventh in adjusted EPA/play on offense. It’s been a wild turnaround, and even though the Ducks have a huge talent surplus, their coaching staff is not in a great place, and Dante Moore is out for the year. The Northwestern playoff push continues on after a big win Saturday. Rob Gregson — A to Z Sports Alabama Prediction: Northwestern 25, Oregon 20 The 2026 Oregon Ducks are a case study in why turnover at the coordinator positions is problematic. That, and why if you can go to the NFL and be a high first-rounder, you should. The loss of Dante Moore for the season underscores what has been a messy situation from start to finish on offense this season. Will Stein has the Wildcats thriving in Kentucky, and that loss is felt in a major way. But the defense hasn’t been much better. Now, a Northwestern squad that is willing to run the ball at will is heading to Oregon, and I think they will challenge the physicality of the Ducks in a major way. Oregon doesn’t have the firepower to score, and it will be a massive win for Northwestern. Craig Smith — A to Z Sports Miami Prediction: Northwestern 23, Oregon 19 Boy, how the perception of this game has changed since Labor Day weekend. Oregon’s playoff goose is cooked at 4-3 after losses to Oklahoma State, UCLA, and Illinois. Dante Moore is done for the season. Offensive coordinator Drew Mehringer was fired after the loss to the Illini. In other words, things are a mess, particularly on the offensive side of the ball. This one stays close at Autzen Stadium, as the Ducks move the ball relatively well early on. But Northwestern, while allowing 364.6 yards per game, has been very good at keeping the point total lower, ranking 22nd nationally at 16.6 points per game. The Wildcats force some early field goals, and their ground game, paced by Caleb Komolafe, takes over the second half as the Wildcats get out of town at 7-1 and firmly in the Big Ten and playoff races. Justin Churchill — A to Z Sports Oklahoma Prediction: Oregon 20, Northwestern 17 Oregon is favored in this matchup currently by a field goal. And I have them winning by just that. Northwestern is a good team, and their story is amazing. But I think Oregon’s overall talent and coaching advantage in this one is just too good. Northwestern does have a +9 turnover margin. They force them, and they don’t commit them. Oregon cannot say the same. They have also scored on 96% of their red zone opportunities this year, which is extremely good. So, I can see why that would be enticing. But this Oregon roster is just too talented to give up on yet. Ryan Roberts — A to Z Sports Notre Dame Prediction: Oregon 21, Northwestern 20 Northwestern has earned plenty of respect with its performance this season, but I’m still leaning toward Oregon to find a way to win at home. The Ducks have endured a difficult stretch, and losing Dante Moore for the season makes an already challenging situation even more complicated. Still, the talent on this roster is difficult to overlook, particularly in a game that could come down to one or two critical possessions. Northwestern’s ability to run the football and protect the ball makes the Wildcats a dangerous opponent, especially against an Oregon team that has struggled to find consistency. However, I expect the Ducks to make just enough plays offensively to survive a tight finish. Northwestern has a legitimate opportunity to pull off the upset, but I’m giving Oregon the narrow edge at Autzen Stadium. Consensus: Can Northwestern Finish the Upset? The A to Z Sports predictions lean heavily toward Northwestern, with four of the five analysts picking the Wildcats to win. The common theme is Oregon’s offensive instability following Dante Moore’s season-ending injury and the coaching changes that have contributed to an uneven campaign. Northwestern’s ability to run the football, limit opponents’ scoring, and capitalize on mistakes gives the Wildcats a path to a major road victory. Justin Churchill and I are the exceptions, backing Oregon to lean on its roster talent and home-field advantage. Both expect a close game, and I am predicting a one-point Ducks victory. Regardless of the final score, Northwestern has an opportunity to turn an impressive start into a season-defining result. Oregon, meanwhile, needs to show that its talent can overcome the problems that have derailed its season. If the Wildcats establish the run and force Oregon into uncomfortable passing situations, an upset in Eugene could be very much in play. What happened instead raises questions about Dan Lanning's program that go beyond one bad game. The 2026 season hasn't gone to plan for the Oregon Ducks , with the team underperforming compared to where it was expected to be. Oregon entered the year with high expectations to go after a title, but the team has faltered this season . The Ducks will be coming into this current week with a record of 4-3, with the team coming off a tough loss to Illinois. This week, the Ducks will be hosting the No. 20-ranked Northwestern Wildcats, offering this group a chance to grab a big win. Northwestern has been a major surprise this season, with the team going 6-1 to open the year. Oregon will be starting quarterback Dylan Raiola in the game, with starter Dante Moore now out for the remainder of the season. Raiola has seen his moments of success with the Ducks this year, but overall, he has struggled to play up to par. Related stories But the Ducks are going to need him to show up against Northwestern for this team to have a chance. Oregon can at least salvage the season a little but if they can pull out a victory at home this weekend. Heading into the game, college football analyst David Kenyon of Bleacher Report put out predictions for the matchups this week. Among these, Kenyon predicted that the Ducks will come away with a slim victory over Northwestern by a score of 21-19. Based on how the Ducks have played over the last few weeks, this seems to be an accurate prediction. Oregon has struggled to find its footing recently, but this is still a good team, especially ay home, where it's tough for opposing teams to play. With Raiola starting, the Ducks coaching staff is going to have to figure out a way to get him into better spots. Raiola has thrown for 761 yards with six touchdowns and two interceptions this season. Oregon fired offensive coordinator Drew Mehringer following the loss to Illinois, and this could help the team be more explosive. Head coach Dan Lanning understood that some type of move needed to be made, and Mehringer ended up being the odd man out here. The Ducks will have to put points on the board to keep up with the explosive Northwestern offense. Quarterback Aidan Chiles has been great for the Wildcards this season, and he could cause real problems for Oregon in this game if the defense isn't careful. The unfortunate 2026 season for the Oregon Ducks continues to get worse by the day, as Dan Lanning announced on Monday that he does not expect quarterback Dante Moore to return this season. Over the past few weeks, Moore had returned to practice for Oregon, participating with the team on a daily basis. But, in terms of returning to the field in an uncontrolled environment, Dan Lanning mentioned that he can not be cleared by the Ducks medical team for a return to live action. "Really got clarity for us over the past week. I think if it was up to Dante in any shape or way, he would want to be out there playing for the guys," Lanning said on Monday. "But unfortunately, it's not really up to Dante, and it's not really up to me. We can control the settting of practice where he's able to do things for us, where that's not always the case in a game. "You know, we said before that this is a serious deal that he'll 100% be able to make a full recovery from. That has not changed, I definitely feel that way. But for him to be out there on the field for us right now, that's not going to happen." "We're getting one of the best scout team looks in practice every week, and he looks good out there," Lanning mentioned. "This isn’t like a selfish decision on Dante's part saying 'I don't wanna come back, the season doesn’t look like theyw ay I want it to look'. That's not at all what this is." The Oregon quarterback has been projected to be a first-round pick next April, after choosing to return for another season in Eugene this past offseason. home.headline: Oregon Ducks players react to losing Dante Moore for the season: ‘It was bad news to hear’
home.blurb: EUGENE — The Oregon Ducks started life in a new normal this week when hopes of quarterback Dante Moore ’s return were extinguished. RELATED : Experts release new Oregon-Northwestern predictions, picks and best bets after Dante Moore officially ruled out for season For four weeks since Moore was struck in the head while sliding to end a run during a 41-27 win at USC, the team watched him return to practice and hoped he would play again. The offense scored just 42 points over the three games he missed. “It was very heartbreaking to hear, but at the same time, we’ve kind of been getting used to other quarterbacks playing,” he said. “So, in terms of football plays and stuff like that, we just got to rock out with what we’ve been doing. So, we’re already used to it, but I feel for him deeply.” This week, the Ducks also fired offensive coordinator Drew Mehringer. His biggest failing was not generating enough offense with a marginal and unsettled offensive line. Dante Moore was also out. Plus, in two games, the Ducks were missing the team’s top two wide receivers, Jeremiah McClellan and Evan Stewart. At Illinois, the Ducks were missing four of their top five wide receivers. Coach Dan Lanning announced on Monday that Moore would miss the remainder of the season . Moore missed three games after entering concussion protocol following a vicious hit to the head on Sept. 26 at USC. The news, relayed to the team on Sunday, left several players devastated as Oregon (4-3, 2-2 Big Ten) prepares to host No. 20 Northwestern (6-1, 3-1) on Saturday. “It was bad news to hear,” Oregon senior tight end Jamari Johnson said. “That was my guy.” Saturday’s 21-10 loss at Illinois pretty much ended the Ducks’ realistic hope of reaching the College Football Playoff. The next day, Moore told the team he wouldn’t be returning to the field. “Of course, that’s something that’s very heartbreaking, being that he was the first guy to even speak to me when I first got here,” sophomore wide receiver Dakorien Moore said. “We got the same last name, to give us even more connection. So, just that bond that we have in general, I feel for him.” Dante Moore led the Ducks to the national semifinals last season, where they lost to Indiana. Soon after, Moore returned to Oregon to develop and chase a national title — a decision Johnson recalled with both fondness and sadness. “That was like one of the first flashbacks I had in my mind when he said (he was done for the season),” Johnson said. “So, it’s my dog, man. home.blurb: David Banks-Imagn Images David Banks-Imagn Images Northwestern Football: Key Injury Updates Ahead of Oregon Alex Kwiatkowski Partner Oct 30, 2026 12:52 AM Published Oct 30, 2026 12:52 AM Northwestern’s latest injury report has Luke Dehnicke off the list, Robert Fitzgerald out and several Wildcats sidelined ahead of Saturday’s matchup against Oregon. With Northwestern preparing to face an Oregon team that will be looking to adjust offensively, having another experienced receiving option available could be important. Dehnicke’s removal from the availability report is an encouraging sign, although his availability should be confirmed closer to kickoff. Fitzgerald, meanwhile, remains out. The safety has been an important part of Northwestern’s defense, and his absence presents another challenge for a unit preparing to face the Ducks on the road. Northwestern’s defense will need to communicate effectively and limit explosive plays as Oregon adjusts to a new offensive play-caller . Brendan Flakes is listed as doubtful, while Robby Preckel remains questionable. Flakes has contributed on special teams, including blocking a key field goal in Northwestern’s win over Michigan State . His potential absence could affect the Wildcats’ special teams depth against Oregon. Several other players remain out, including offensive lineman Ezomo Oratokhai, Josh Fussell, Daniel Anderson, Max Mohring, Jason Reynolds II, Callen Campbell, Qayvier Johnson, Jacob Miller and Chris Petrucci. Braxton Strong is also listed as out after previously being listed as doubtful. With several players still sidelined, Northwestern will need contributions from across its roster. Dehnicke’s potential return would provide a welcome boost, while the defense must find ways to compensate for Fitzgerald’s absence as the Wildcats look to extend their winning streak. Wide receiver Nyck Harbor is a big-play threat at any moment. Defensively, Dylan Stewart wreaks havoc on most offenses he faces — he's recorded two sacks and forced three fumbles in four games this season. The Sooners will likely need kicker Tate Sandell to be better, though. It's been a combination of running back Matt Fuller and quarterback LaNorris Sellers on the ground. Fuller has 513 yards and five touchdowns. away.blurb: On offense, key players Ryan Fodje and Eddy Pierre-Louis aren't close to returning and were ruled out. However, guard Heath Ozaeta could make his first appearance since the win over Texas. Ozaeta was listed as probable. If he's able to play, he provides Oklahoma a valuable piece to its interior offensive line rotation. If he's able to play, it's likely Ozaeta slides back into the starting lineup, though he could platoon with Peyton Joseph, who has had ups and downs for the Sooners the last two weeks. It also looks like running back Xavier Robinson could be available this week. The Carl Albert High School graduate hasn't played since the Week 4 loss to Georgia and played fewer than 10 snaps in back-to-back weeks before suffering a calf strain. He'll battle with Jonathan Hatton for the third running back carries as Lloyd Avant and Tory Blaylock have established themselves as the Sooners' 1-2 punch in the running back rotation. If he can't play, it'll be Omarion Robinson and Michael Boganowski starting at the safety spots, and potentially Reggie Powers mixing into the rotation. If Eli Bowen is out, Trystan Haynes would likely get another start. He's been solid since entering the starting lineup against the Texas Longhorns and would need to be at his best this week if called upon to start. Injuries have once again been a key storyline for the Sooners in the 2026 season. If the key players listed as questionable and probable can be available for this week, it would give the Sooners a boost on both sides of the football. picks.blurb: Clemson (4-3, 3-2 ACC) is coming off a last-minute 20-16 loss to the Virginia Tech Hokies at Memorial Stadium. The Tigers led for much of the second half, but Hokies quarterback Ethan Grunkemeyer led his team on an 11-play, 69-yard drive for the game-winning score with 1:44 to play. Grunkmeyer's 5-yard touchdown pass to tight end Luke Reynolds on fourth-and-1 gave Virginia Tech its first win over Clemson in 19 years and dropped the Tigers to 2-8 in their last 10 home games against Power Four opponents. The offense struggled once again, netting only 288 total yards and going 3 of 14 on third downs. Freshman QB Tait Reynolds completed 20 of his 26 passes, but his average completion went for only 5.9 yards. The Tigers rank dead last in the ACC and just 115th nationally in total offense with 333.1 yards per game. Clemson will face a Florida State (3-4, 1-3) team fresh off a bye, and one that should be playing with plenty of confidence. Mike Norvell's Seminoles took the top-ranked Miami Hurricanes into double overtime before falling 43-35 at Hard Rock Stadium on Oct. 17. Fifth-year senior Ashton Daniels leads the Seminoles' passing attack and has 1,618 yards and 12 touchdowns to eight interceptions in seven games this season. Daniels threw four touchdown passes and rushed for another score in FSU's loss to Miami in Week 7. Clemson has won nine of the last 10 meetings against Florida State dating back to 2015. Neither program wants to move on from its coach and pay a hefty buyout, but neither team has shown very much on the field lately to offer hope. The Tigers suffered a 20-16 gut-punch loss to Virginia Tech in Week 8. It marked Clemson's eighth in its last 10 games against a Power Four opponent at home. The Tigers led for much of the second half until Ethan Grunkemeyer's game-winning 5-yard touchdown pass on fourth-and-1 with 1:44 left. Florida State came within a play or two of adding to the chaos that was college football's thrilling Week 7 slate. The Seminoles took Miami to double overtime before falling 43-35 at Hard Rock Stadium. FSU quarterback Ashton Daniels accounted for five touchdowns in the loss, including four through the air. Clemson hasn't thrown four touchdowns all season. Tait Reynolds, the 19-year-old true freshman who was thrust into the starting job following an injury to Christopher Vizzina, is averaging just 6.1 yards per completion and has been sacked 20 times in seven games behind a weak offensive line. Clemson ranks 115th nationally in total offense with 333.1 yards per game, which is last in the ACC. Florida State ranks 49th with 414.3 total yards per games. Here's ESPN's prediction for Saturday's game. Will Clemson football beat Florida State? ESPN's final score prediction Ahead of Clemson-Florida State, ESPN's Bill Connelly predicted the final score using his popular SP+ metrics . Connelly has the Seminoles winning their first game against the Tigers at Doak Campbell Stadium since 2014. The oddsmakers' latest 5.5 spread favors FSU, as well. Connelly's final score prediction: Florida State 27, Clemson 24. He gives the Seminoles a win probability of 59%. The Tigers have an overall rating of 4.7, up from 4.0 a week ago. Clemson is one spot ahead of UCF in ESPN's overall team rankings. To break down Clemson's rating by unit, SP+ gives the Tigers a 23.3 rating on offense (No. 97 nationally, up one spot from last week) and a 19.0 rating on defense, which is 25th nationally and is the same as before the Tigers' loss to the Hokies. In special teams, Clemson has a 0.5 rating, which ranks 10th-best in the nation. Florida State is No. 54 in the SP+ team rankings with an overall rating of 5.8, one spot below Virginia and one ahead of Clemson. The metrics give the Seminoles a 32.7 rating on offense that's No. 32 nationally, a 27.1 rating on defense that's No. 76, and a 0.2 rating in special teams that's 43rd in the country. What are ESPN SP+ rankings? According to Connelly, SP+ is "simply a measure of the most sustainable and predictable aspects of football. If you're lucky or unimpressive in a win, your rating will probably fall. If you're strong and unlucky in a loss, it will probably rise." "SP+ is not a résumé ranking, so it does not automatically give credit for big wins or particularly brave scheduling -- no good predictive system does," he adds. The kickoff is scheduled for 7:00 p.m., and the game will be televised by the ACCN. This will be the 39th meeting between the teams, with Florida State (3-4, 1-3 ACC) leading the all-time series 21-17, including a 12-7 record at Doak and an 18-15 record as ACC members. However, Clemson has won the last two meetings and holds a 15-7 advantage over the last 22 games, including wins in nine of the last 10 meetings. Clemson will be attempting to win a fifth consecutive game at Doak, becoming only the third program ever to win five consecutive road games against FSU in Tallahassee, joining Florida (six straight from 1966-76) and Miami (Fla.) (five from 1957-77). Despite Clemson (4-3, 2-2 ACC) and Florida State combining for 13 of the last 15 ACC championships, both teams are struggling this year. Clemson’s losses have come against #15 LSU, #1 Miami, and a 6-2 Virginia Tech team that scored the winning touchdown with 1:44 left on the clock. FSU’s four losses were in double overtime at #1 Miami, at #10 Alabama, at home against #19 SMU, and at Louisville when the defense totally collapsed. Clemson’s defense is the strength of their team. The Tigers rank 32nd in total defense (317), 36th in passing (186), T-53rd in rushing defense (131), T-30th in third-down defense (holding opponents to a 33.3-percent conversion rate), have allowed only four passing touchdowns, and have recorded 20 sacks through seven games. The Tigers’ passing offense, behind true freshman QB Tait Reynolds, who was named starter following an injury to Christopher Vizzina in their 2nd game, has only thrown one touchdown, and the 2 QBs combined have only thrown 2 TDs all season. Reynolds has been sacked 20 times this season and has thrown 3 interceptions while averaging just 6.1 yards per completion. Overall, Clemson has allowed 21 sacks, rank 115th in total offense (333). 112th in scoring offense, 115th in passing offense, 126th in 3rd-down conversion (31.7%), and 93rd in red zone offense. Florida State looks to avoid its 3rd straight loss after a heartbreaking double-overtime loss to Miami. The Noles were able to rush for 138 yards against the nation’s #1-ranked rushing defense; however, leading rusher Ousmane Kromah sustained a lower-leg injury and will miss the rest of the 2026 season. I imagine that, off a bye, head coach Mike Norvell will scheme up points on the opening drive, and Tony White’s defense should make forcing CU to throw the name of the game. This game will be close, as it often is with FSU, but Clemson isn’t good enough right now to win a rivalry game on the road. Seminole win, but no cover. FSU 27, Clemson 24 Tim Scribble (season record: 6-1) This could be a scary game, fitting for Halloween. With Kromah out, Clemson’s defense may keep FSU in check but the Tiger’s offense is dreadful. If Clemson somehow overwhelm’s Tony White’s defense, that relationship needs to end. I think FSU wins but it will be ugly. FSU 24, Clemson 17 Jacob Smith (season record: 3-2 ) Call me crazy, but this game is going to be completely unwatchable but FSU will emerge victorious. Firstly, it’s at Doak. On Halloween. Where else would you rather be? In all seriousness, Clemson’s offensive efficiency is dreadful. Like, REALLY dreadful. Per Game On Paper , Clemson’s EPA per pass is #136 out of #138 and their EPA per rush is #110. They are only 33.7% successful on third down, good for #128, and they are just bad at most things offense, mainly because their QB is a freshman. Their defense is good to great, though! #13 in EPA/Pass defense and just middle of the pack on rushing defense, #64 in the nation. Florida State meanwhile… their defense is trash. #127 on EPA per pass, #105 on EPA per rush, #120 on 3rd/4th down stops. The offense is good, though. #39 in EPA/Pass, #36 in EPA/Rush. If they can handle Clemson’s terrible offense and do good things on defense against a very not good Clemson offense, it might be a fun halloweekend in Tallahassee. Give me the Noles to pull off, not an upset per se, just a good, scrappy win. Florida State 14, Clemson 13 Curt Weiler (season record: 5-2, 2-5 ATS) Call me crazy for buying in again but I think I believe in this FSU team more than I do that Clemson team. The Tigers’ defense is pretty good. But the offense is very bad. Clemson is the only FBS team which has scored more points from its defense/special teams than its offense . To Tony White and his unit, I would say “If not now, when?” FSU 27, Clemson 20 NoleThruandThru (season record: 7-0) I’m taking a break from the Marshawn gag this week to honor my dad, who passed away two weeks ago. The world lost a wonderful FSU alum and fan, and I hope he enjoys this one from heaven. FSU 28, Clemson 24 Jon Marchant (season record: 6-1 ) Nobody knows what kind of team FSU will be from week to week. No result is off the table and there’s no score that would surprise anyone. So I’m picking FSU this week. Just cause. Also, it’s funny when Dabo loses. Clemson 23, FSU 28 LastNoleOfKrypton (season record: 5-1) I’m picking FSU but I don’t feel great about the prediction. I’m really worried about what FSU’s offense will look like without Kromah vs. Clemson’s defense. That being said I have not seen enough from Clemson’s offense to stay off the field and if you give FSU’s skill group enough shots they’re going to get points. Noles win. FSU 24 Clemson 17 Matt Minnick (Season record: 5-2; ATS: 4-3) As others have said, Clemson’s offense is putrid. Two passing touchdowns all season long is nearly unfathomable. But is Tony White’s defense just what the doctor ordered? It’s the moveable object vs the stoppable force. I’ve said all year that despite all the suckage over the last three seasons, FSU has honestly been pretty decent at home. However, Norvell’s teams also have a penchant for finding ways to lose very winnable games. If Kromah was healthy, I’d feel a lot better about the ‘Noles. If Quindarious Jones was healthy I’d feel a lot better about the ‘Noles. If a random FCS DC who’s name was drawn out of a hat was FSU’s defensive coordinator, I’d feel a lot better about the ‘Noles. Clemson 30 , FSU 28 Frank DNole (season record: 3-4) FSU’s offense is better than Clemson’s defense. Clemson’s offense is about as good as FSU’s defense. Advantage Noles. This will be the game that turns the program around, and everything comes together for the Noles. The Noles are 5.5-point favorites for a reason. Vegas knows something and the Seminoles know it too. The game will follow a similar storyline to what we witnessed against Virginia. The Seminoles will win the offensive, defensive, and special teams battles because the FSU players will give 110% more effort, they will want it more, and they will play with more heart than their equally talented Clempsun opponent. FSU Seminoles 34, Orange Dabo’s 27 P erry Kostidakis (season record: 4-3, 3-4 ATS) For all its flaws over the last two seasons, FSU has taken care of business against the teams it should beat while in the confines of Doak. I have faith in FSU’s ability to get enough points against a stout Clemson defense and, as naive as it might be, take care of business against a dreadful Tigers offense. away.headline: Two FSU freshmen trending toward returning vs. Clemson
away.blurb: Crutchfield has been in and out of FSU's lineup this season as he battles injuries, but the coaching staff has been extremely pleased with what he can do, and Norvell is "hopeful" he will be available this week. "I think Jordan Crutchfield is trending well to be able to get back in the secondary," Norvell said. "We've had some guys that have been banged up there as well. Jordan's a guy that has shown some flashes here, just dealt with some minor injuries that have kind of set him back just from the consistency of his opportunities, but expecting him to get some good work here this week and hopefully be available." The update was less positive about Nichelson, who hasn't played since the game against the New Mexico State Aggies, and Norvell doesn't expect that to change this week. He is "hopeful" that the rest of the linebackers will be able to play after several were in and out of the Miami game with injuries. home.headline: Florida State injury updates: Mike Norvell expects key returns, but timing is an issue
home.blurb: Florida State coach Mike Norvell recently provided a couple of injury updates on multiple Seminoles who have missed significant time this season. Injuries have been a huge issue for the team this year for Norvell, particularly on defense, where multiple players are out for the season. Sometimes injuries can make or break a team, and so far, the Seminoles have been able to do quite a bit with multiple contributors sidelined. Norvell kicked off his injury updates portion of the press conference with a quick tidbit on linebacker Blake Nichelson, who has not played since the season opener against New Mexico State. Nichelson is nearing a return, and while the game against Clemson might still be out of reach , the linebacker should be able to return to play soon. Samuel Singleton Jr.'s return would be huge for the Florida State offense Norvell is not giving up on Singleton's return; he never ruled the running back out for the season, and he clearly still thinks there is hope for his return. It might be a delusion at this point from Norvell to avoid the reality that Florida State is in a bad spot at running back, or a future return this season might still truly be in the cards. I personally would like to think that Singleton is close to coming back, and the faster he can return, the better for Florida State. Tre Wisner is an experienced running back, but he has not been the most effective player in a short sample size this season. Aside from Wisner, there is not much of an experienced supporting cast. Additionally, Florida State might be in trouble if Singleton is not able to return this season due to the fact that there are only three healthy running backs. The Seminoles truly cannot afford to have another running back go down with an injury, and if Singleton is not available for another two or three weeks, that could be an issue. The timing of Crutchfield's return could not be any better, with Quindarrius Jones, Nehemiah Chandler, and Ashlynd Barker all dealing with injuries. Barker has been playing through his injury thanks to a cast, but Crutchfield can do it all in the secondary, and he should be able to take some pressure off multiple players. picks.blurb: UNC vs Miami prediction: Will Bill Belichick's Tar Heels upset No. 1 Hurricanes? - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NCAAF College Fantasy Football College Football Playoff Packers defeat Panthers WNBA Finals: Dream force Game 7 Bears land DT Jeffery Simmons HS player bodychecks ref Red Wings suspend Larkin Rodd Baxley, Fayetteville Observer Fri, October 30, 2026 at 9:04 AM UTC · 4 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads For the first time in 22 years, UNC football is hosting a top-five Miami team on Halloween weekend at Kenan Stadium. Bill Belichick's Tar Heels (4-3, 2-2 ACC) host the top-ranked Hurricanes (7-0, 5-0) on Saturday, Oct. 31 (7:30 p.m., ABC), with hopes of earning the program's first victory against the No. 1 team in the nation. UNC earned a 31-28 against No. 4 Miami on Halloween weekend in 2004, getting a game-winning field goal from Wilmington native Connor Barth. The Tar Heels are aiming for their sixth straight win against the Hurricanes, who haven't beaten UNC since 2018. But the Heels are 0-11 in games against the top-ranked team in the country. Watch UNC-Miami on Fubo RED-ZONE PROBLEM: UNC football red-zone rate doesn't tell full story for Bill Belichick's Tar Heels "Miami, they're the No. 1 team in the country and they should be," UNC coach Bill Belichick said during his weekly press conference. "Really impressive. (Miami coach Mario Cristobal has) done, as usual, a great job down there. They're a very well-balanced team, pretty much do everything well." Here are some things to know, players to watch and a score prediction for UNC vs. Miami. Miami QB Darian Mensah, Miami WR Malachi Toney are Heisman Trophy hopefuls Conversations about the Hurricanes start with quarterback Darian Mensah and wide receiver Malachi Toney, two players hoping to be in New York City for the Heisman Trophy ceremony. Mensah leads the nation in completion percentage (81.4%) with 22 touchdowns and one interception. Toney paces all pass-catchers with 66 catches for 952 yards and 11 TDs. If UNC fans want a sign of hope, Mensah was limited to 175 passing yards and a touchdown last season for Duke vs. the Tar Heels. Still, this Miami offense is operating in a different stratosphere with an average of nearly 50 points per game. Mark Fletcher, Miami rushing offense can't be overlooked by UNC In addition to a potent passing attack, Miami has the 18th rushing offense nationally at 211 yards per game. The Hurricanes have gained at least 119 rushing yards in each of their seven games, including more than 257 yards against Florida State. Running backs Mark Fletcher and Javian Mallory have combined for 858 yards and 14 rushing TDs, averaging nearly 7 yards per carry. The Tar Heels are 91st in rushing defense, allowing an average of nearly 155 yards per game on the ground. The last time it played a top-five opponent, UNC allowed No. 5 Notre Dame to rack up 241 rushing yards. UNC defense, special teams need special play to beat Hurricanes If the Tar Heels are going to pull off an upset against the Hurricanes, it'll likely involve a special play from the defense or special teams. UNC made it a one-point game against Notre Dame with a game-changing kickoff return for a touchdown and nearly had a ice-the-game fumble recovery for a TD in a win at Pitt. With eight takeaways (5 interceptions, 3 fumble recoveries), UNC is 75th nationally. The Heels have to create some chaos for the Hurricanes to keep the crowd in it and put some game pressure on the visitors. UNC vs Miami score prediction Miami 38, UNC 18 : The Tar Heels have improved enough to close in on bowl eligibility, but the Hurricanes are in a different neighborhood as national championship contenders. In what will serve as a gauge-where-we-are game for Bill Belichick's program, "The U" will pull away in the second half. away.headline: Notre Dame can survive its latest injury wave against Navy, but Miami is different
away.blurb: Notre Dame football’s “ next man up ” philosophy should be enough to get Marcus Freeman through Navy despite another crowded injury report. But with DJ McKinney out, Brauntae Johnson still sidelined, and Kyngstonn Viliamu-Asa among the questionable players, Chris Ash needs that list to shrink considerably before Miami arrives. Despite the Fighting Irish coming off a bye week , head coach Marcus Freeman detailed several injuries that will hit Chris Ash’s unit hard. The good news is that none of the players who will miss time or be questionable are ones the team should need against Navy. The question is how healthy some of these guys will be in two weeks against Miami. On Monday afternoon, Freeman said McKinney is out for the Navy game with an ankle injury. That’s never good news, as that kind of injury can stick around for a while. A cornerback who can’t make cuts won’t keep up with receivers. That’s not an issue against Navy, but against Miami, especially Malachi Toney, it’s a big one. Another big injury update: safety Brauntae Johnson is still out. Notre Dame has hoped he’d be out for “just a couple of weeks” after he was injured in the first half of the season opener. However, with the season now in Week 8, people have to start worrying about whether he will play this year. The injury list doesn’t end there. Freeman said that tight end Cooper Flanagan (hamstring), linebacker Kyngstonn Viliamu-Asa (thumb), defensive lineman Loghan Thomas (shoulder), and cornerback Mark Zackery IV (concussion) are all questionable. Of course, of all the injuries that might just be cautionary, KVA’s questionable status is the most likely situation where he could have been fine to play if Miami was this week. Notre Dame should absolutely be able to beat Navy even without Viliamu-Asa in the lineup. The injury that should make Notre Dame faithful most worried is DJ McKinney’s. The transfer cornerback was hurt late in the game against BYU , and the bye week apparently wasn't enough time for him to heal and get back to 100%. Notre Dame football defensive injuries create bigger questions for Miami than Navy Because Notre Dame knows Navy won’t tax its cornerbacks much, sitting McKinney this week isn’t a shock. It’s even possible that if this were Miami week , they’d be working to get him back on the field. The Irish won’t push it against the Midshipmen. The most interesting note in that group is that Notre Dame took quite a bit of heat for not playing Viliamu-Asa more against BYU. It’s clear now that one reason he wasn’t in the game more was that his thumb was still bothering him. home.headline: North Carolina Dealing With Unknown Injury to Matt Able
home.blurb: I'd be worried if he doesn't play a lot in the first month or so, though. UNC has a need to get better as a team with all the new faces and a different system. The last thing the program needs is for one of the best players on the roster to be out. North Carolina Dealing With Unknown Injury to Matt Able TarHeelsRoundtable 160 Members • 1,565 Posts TarHeelsRoundtable TarHeelsRoundtable Related stories IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect North Carolina Dealing With Unknown Injury to Matt Able Jon Conahan Partner Oct 29, 2026 4:00 PM Published Oct 29, 2026 4:00 PM Able has to get healthy for UNC. North Carolina fans are ready for the college basketball season, but a couple of things need to be considered before Monday night as it takes on Western Carolina. North Carolina should be able to win this game no matter who's on the court for them, but it's also important to note that some injuries are currently being factored in. The biggest is Matt Able, the North Carolina State transfer expected to be one of the better players on the roster this season. Able missed the exhibition game against Charlotte, though it hasn't been reported yet what happened. According to Rodd Baxley, who was at the game, the injury didn't look noticeable. Baxley added that he was on the sidelines during UNC's warmups, and it didn't seem to be too big of a problem. “Able, an N.C. State transfer, is one of 11 newcomers on coach Michael Malone's first roster in Chapel Hill. The 6-foot-5, 200-pound guard is a starter in the backcourt alongside Virginia Tech transfer Neo Avdalas and Utah transfer Terrence Brown… “Able's injury doesn't look noticeable. He was on the sidelines during UNC's warmups ahead of the game. Still, it's another missed opportunity for Able to get game action with a revamped roster and a backcourt that includes Utah transfer Terrence Brown, along with Virginia Tech transfer Neo Avdalas. Isaiah Denis missed the Indiana exhibition game with a minor injury,” Baxley wrote . Able, who withdrew from the NBA draft last year to go to North Carolina, is expected to be one of the ACC's better players this season. He's coming off a decent freshman year at NC State, averaging 8.8 points, 3.4 rebounds, and shooting 35.5% from three-point range on 4.1 attempts per game. He has areas to improve, including as a passer, but there's a lot to like about the young man, and the hope is that he'll be what everybody knows he can be. Hopefully, this is just a small thing, and North Carolina can get it under control before it plays on Monday night. If not, it's fine if he misses a few games.

home.headline: Miami returns to all-white stormtroopers for Halloween Night trip to North Carolina
home.blurb: Miami returns to all-white stormtroopers for Halloween night trip to North Carolina Skip to main content About Hurricanes All-Time Football Lists Hurricanes All-Time Basketball Lists Miami Hurricanes Basketball Recruiting The Joe Gaither Show on CanesCentral The Miami Hurricanes will wear their all-white "Stormtrooper" combination for Saturday night's Halloween game against the North Carolina Tar Heels. Miami announced the look on Thursday, pairing white helmets with white jerseys and white pants (the program's standard road uniform). The No. 1 Hurricanes are undefeated in the combination this season after road wins at Stanford (45-6), Wake Forest (33-20) and Clemson (41-13). All white, all business 🙌 pic.twitter.com/dpVbfdILLx North Carolina enters at 4-3 overall and 2-2 in ACC play, while Miami (7-0, 5-0 ACC) arrives as a two-touchdown favorite. The Hurricanes are seeking their first win in Chapel Hill since 2017 and first victory in the series since 2018. North Carolina has won the past five meetings and holds a series edge 16-11. The Hurricanes have largely stuck to a simple rotation. The all-white Stormtroopers have served as the primary road look, and at home they have worn the traditional white helmet, orange jersey and white pants combination against Florida A&M and Florida State. The green alternate (white helmet, green jersey, green pants) appeared once, in a 52-3 win over Central Michigan. Last week against Pittsburgh, Miami debuted the home version of its 2001 Tribute throwbacks to honor the 25th anniversary of the 2001 national championship team. The road version of those throwbacks (white jersey with green pants) has not yet been used. They have met 24 times in their history, though a lot of those meetings have come in bowl games. In fact, they have played nearly as many games against one another in Pasadena at the Rose Bowl (7) as they have in Los Angeles at the Coliseum (8). What they have not done, however, is face each other as conference mates. Their last meeting came in the 2017 Cotton Bowl. Prior to that, they hadn't played since the 2009 season. It took until USC's third season as a Big Ten member for the two to appear on each other's schedules, but this Saturday night the wait will end. And it's a game that got a lot more intriguing in recent weeks. USC enters the game unranked for the first time all season following a 17-7 loss at Wisconsin last week. While Ohio State remains second in the AP Top 25, this will be the team's first game since losing starting quarterback Julian Sayin , who was knocked out of their 19-15 win over Indiana . Ohio State vs. USC: Need to know This will be Luke Fahey's first career start: On the surface, giving your quarterback his first career start on the road is not an ideal situation, but it's one Ohio State has had success with before. In 2001, Craig Krenzel started his first game on the road against Michigan of all teams, and Ohio State won that game 26-20. In 2013, it was Kenny Guiton winning his first start at Cal, and in 2021, CJ Stroud won his first start at Minnesota . There's a lot on the line for Jeremiah Smith : Smith is the best receiver in the country and is already Ohio State's all-time leader in career receptions, yards, and touchdowns, just to name a few stats. He's also the clear favorite to win the Heisman Trophy, but this will be his first start with Fahey as well. It's safe to assume Smith will be Fahey's preferred target, but it remains to be seen whether he can maintain the same level of production and how that may impact his Heisman chances. USC is 9-2 at home in Big Ten games since joining the league: I started with the good part. The bad news is that the Trojans are only 1-2 at home in Big Ten games against ranked opponents. They're 5-14 overall against ranked teams under Lincoln Riley, and Jayden Maiava is 1-5 as a starter against them. The lone win came last season at home against Michigan. Riley, who is 41-20 at USC and carries a reported $70 million buyout , addressed his future Tuesday. “This is where I want to be. This is the right place for me. I’m the right person to be here ,” he said. Davis expects a lopsided result to add to that conversation, though he cautioned USC against a quick change. “Ohio State goes in there and rolls and creates even more discussion around the future of USC,” Davis said. “Although, be very careful. You don’t know that you’re going to get someone that’s better. It’s not like Lincoln Riley’s a bad coach. It just hasn’t been quite to the level that they’ve expected up to this point.” Kickoff at the Los Angeles Memorial Coliseum is set for 7:30 p.m. ET Saturday on NBC. Sayin's absence remains the biggest concern after the quarterback suffered a throwing-arm injury during Ohio State's 19-15 victory over Indiana on Oct. 17. Sayin, who threw for 2,007 yards and 19 touchdowns this season, is expected to be out indefinitely. Who's on deck for the Buckeyes? The uncertainty is compounded by the fact that head coach Ryan Day has not officially named a starter. As of Thursday, both freshman Luke Fahey and redshirt freshman Tavien St. Clair were preparing to play against USC. Fahey has completed nine of 13 passes for 203 yards with two touchdowns and two interceptions; St. Clair has attempted only seven passes. The counterargument is Ohio State's defense, which allows just 13.4 points per game, and the presence of star receiver Jeremiah Smith. The Heisman favorite has 984 receiving yards and 12 touchdowns. Those strengths help explain why the Buckeyes remain heavily favored by predictive models. Still, a 13-point projection assumes Ohio State can maintain much of its usual efficiency despite a major change at the sport's most important position. Until Fahey or St. Clair proves capable of directing the offense for four quarters, that margin looks ambitious. Ohio State is still the better team, but expecting the Buckeyes to win comfortably in their first game without Sayin is a bold call.

It's among the most super of superpowers. It's one of those programs with no excuses. It gets just about any player it wants, its realistic expectations are national title or bust, and it's one of the few programs that can lose its starting quarterback and still reasonably be considered the No. 1 team in the country. But now it has to go at least the next several weeks without star quarterback Julian Sayin, who injured his shoulder in the win over Indiana a few weeks ago. There's a quarterback battle to see who steps into the role as the team travels to Los Angeles to face a desperate USC team in a whole lot of trouble. The Trojans are 6-2, but they just got stuffed by Wisconsin in a punishing 24-7 loss, and with a brutal schedule to close, the Lincoln Riley hot seat is flaming. On the plus side, win, and the team is still deep in the College Football Playoff hunt. Ohio State vs USC: Quick Hits It doesn't get any easier for USC with a trip to Indiana next after a week off, and then Maryland, and it all closes at UCLA. Ohio State finishes with three of its last four games in Columbus, hosting Oregon next week. The road game is at Nebraska. This is the first time these two have met since a 24-7 Ohio State win in the 2017 Cotton Bowl. USC has won seven or the last eight in the series goning back to the 1974 Rose Bowl. How To Watch Ohio State vs USC Date: Saturday, October 31, 2026 Game Time: 7:30 PM ET TV: NBC Location: Los Angeles Memorial Coliseum, Los Angeles, CA – Week 9 Schedule, Game Previews – CFN Top 25 | Bowl Projections – Predicting the First CFP Top 25 – CFN Week 9 Expert Picks Why Ohio State Will Win USC just isn't that great. It has a wonderful 6-2 record, quarterback Jayden Maiava is terrific, and there's still pop and explosion to worry about, but there are flaws. It beat Washington and Penn State, but lost at home to a struggling Oregon, and couldn't get anything going against the Badgers. Ohio State isn't the Ohio State of previous seasons, but it's still good enough to beat anyone else this year. To win, the Buckeyes have to screw up, but USC doesn't take the ball away with just six turnovers forced on the season, and there's little running game to worry about. USC ran well on Rutgers and Louisiana, and that's about it. Slow down the midrange USC passing game, slow down USC. Why USC Will Win If Ohio State didn't exactly go turn-it-loose full-throttle with Julian Sayin under center, what will it do with Luke Fahey and/or Tavien St. Clair? Both are talented prospects, and no matter who is under center, there's still Jeremiah Smith and a loaded receiving corps to throw to, but this is where the offense has to rely on the running game, and it might not be able to do it. The Buckeyes are averaging a pedestrian four yards per carry, and were stuffed by Indiana two weeks ago, gaining just 37 yards. Fahey missed both of his throws against Indiana, and St. Clair has only seen the lightest of mop-up work so far. Ohio State vs USC Prediction, Betting Lines Which team has another gear? Can USC's run defense ball out, and can Jayden Maiava play like the best quarterback on the field? Or will the Ohio State defense step up and keep the big pass plays to a minimum? Yes, Indiana came within a few inches from beating Ohio State, but Josh Hoover only hit 50% of his passes, and only Arch Manning has been able to complete more than 56% against the Buckeyes. Maiava will have a nice day, but the Trojans will stall a bit too often. It won't be pretty, but the Buckeyes will take advantage of a few good field position chances to survive and advance in a relatively low-scoring game. After a bye week, the Buckeyes will now be facing off against the USC Trojans, giving this team another test to overcome. Ohio State remains one of the better teams in the country, but the Trojans will be a challenge. This will be the first game between the two historic programs in Big Ten play, giving each another reason to want to win. The two programs have met multiple times over the years, and it's always been a fun matchup. The Buckeyes did lose starting quarterback Julian Sayin, likely for the season, but this team still has a lot of talent on the roster. Ohio State believes that it can still win a title this season, and the Trojans are just the next team in its way. As the team gets ready for the Trojans, they will be entering the game with a record of 6-1, going 4-0 in Big Ten play. USC comes in with a record of 6-2, going 3-2 in their conference games so far. The Trojans are coming off a bad loss to the Wisconsin Badgers last weekend, giving this team all the desperation they need. The Buckeyes will need to stay focused in this game, looking at this trip as purely business. Entering the game, the Buckeyes are still favored to take down the Trojans, even with the injury to Sayin. According to the ESPN matchup predictor , Ohio State has an 82.8 percent chance of defeating USC on the road this week. For the Buckeyes, making sure to keep the basics the same in this game will be a key. Even without Sayin, the offense should still run through star wide receiver Jeremiah Smith, giving the team a boost. Ohio State may rely even more heavily on Smith to help whoever is under center for this Buckeyes team, giving them a reliable target. Smith is on pace for a truly special season, and the loss of Sayin shouldn't change that fact. The Buckeyes defense will also be tasked with slowing down USC quarterback Jayden Maiava, who has thrown for 2,302 yards with 19 touchdowns and five interceptions. The Trojans rely on their offense to set the tone for the team, and the defense has been a little shaky this season. Kickoff between the two sides is scheduled for 4:30 p.m. PT/7:30 p.m. ET from the Los Angeles Memorial Coliseum.

picks.headline: Know Thy Foe: Baylor Expert Shares What UCF Fans Need To Know For Space Game
picks.blurb: Know Thy Foe: Baylor Expert Shares What UCF Fans Need To Know For Space Game Skip to main content SI.COM FOOTBALL RECRUITING COLLEGE FOOTBALL NEWS Olympic Sports More from UCF Knights On SI FOOTBALL While the UCF Knights may be coming off of one of the most significant wins in its program's history against No. 2 BYU on Saturday, they do not have long before they have to follow it up. The Baylor Bears may be entering their first game of the post-Dave Aranda era after firing him on Sunday, but they still have the same record as the Knights, and their interim coach, Joe Klanderman, has been in charge of a defense that has been one of the top five in the nation in sacks and tackles for loss. Jacob Haddaadin is both a Baylor graduate and a contributor for Baylor Bears on SI, and he took some time this week to answer some of our questions about the Bears (4-3, 2-2 Big 12): 1. How did the Bears reach a position in which they ended up firing their head coach midseason? Haddadin: Dave Aranda’s firing wasn't strictly due to this season's results. Ever since Dave Aranda won the Big 12 championship in 2021, the program has slowly trended downward. The Bears had real momentum after beating ASU in Tempe, but that momentum stalled after a double-digit home loss to TCU and a loss to a bad Kansas team in Lawrence. Dave Aranda had a losing record in the Big 12, a 1-6 record against rival TCU, and his teams were consistently unprepared in big games. We are forever grateful for the 12-2 season in 2021, but enough was enough, and Baylor fans were fed up with the constant expectation and disappointment cycle that was Dave Aranda. The loss to Kansas solidified that the Dave Aranda-led team was once again not going to be anything special. Cementing his exit from the program. 2. What’s the rundown on interim coach Joe Klanderman? What made him the choice to lead the program for the remainder of the season? Haddadin: Before Manhattan, Klanderman cut his teeth at North Dakota State, where he spent five years as defensive backs coach from 2014 to 2018, contributing to four FCS national championships. He then spent seven years at Kansas State, six of them running the defense, and K-State maintained a top-30 national ranking in defensive efficiency for five straight seasons through 2025. Part of what made him the choice is continuity. He was brought to Waco as one of the big offseason moves meant to turn things around; he’s already in the building, and the defense he built has been the most reliable part of this team. He has also come in with a clear plan, laying out three priorities for his time as interim head coach: energizing the program, strengthening the roster for 2027, and establishing complementary football to help Baylor win more games. He has been honest about where the problems are, too, pointing to the offensive line and the running game as the areas that need the most work. Whether or not this turns into a permanent job, the next five games give him a real chance to make his case, starting with a Friday night road game at UCF. 3. Quarterback DJ Lagway seems to have really connected with wide receiver Gavin Freeman, the latter of which is second in the nation in receptions per game and 14th in the nation in receiving yards. What makes Freeman such an oft-target wideout? Also, is there anyone else in the Bears’ receiving corps that could step up as a main target if Freeman is well-covered? Haddadin: Gavin Freeman’s production makes sense once you look at what he brings. At 5-9 and 189 pounds, he isn’t going to win many jump balls, but he has been reliable all season. He arrived as a redshirt senior after playing 2022-23 at Oklahoma and 2024-25 at Oklahoma State, and he was already a go-to receiver before coming to Waco, leading the Cowboys with 53 receptions for 481 yards and four scores in 2025. His fit with Lagway was clear from the first game, when he caught 12 passes for 154 yards and a touchdown in his Baylor debut against Auburn. It also helps that during the offseason, observers expected the passing game to work the middle of the field more, since Lagway is more comfortable there than Sawyer Robertson was. That is exactly where a quick, shifty slot receiver like Freeman does his best work. He has also produced when the offense hasn’t: in the 17-6 loss to TCU, he still caught seven passes for 76 yards. He adds value in other ways too. Last year at Oklahoma State, he contributed in both the passing and running game and as a returner. If defenses focus on Freeman, the most likely next option is Louis Brown IV. Before the season, he was described as the leader of the receiver room as one of its few upperclassmen with real experience in the offense, and he and Lagway connected well in the spring. Jadon Porter is another option to watch, and Baylor’s tight ends have been factors in the red zone. 4. Baylor is one of the most penalized teams in the Big 12. Is there one side of the ball that draws more flags? If so, why? Also, is there a particular penalty that gets called a lot? Haddadin: Most of the flags come from the offense, and specifically the offensive line. Through the early home stretch, one count found that the offense was outpacing the defense by nearly 3 to 1 in total penalties. The penalty that keeps showing up is the false start. Baylor had 5 against Prairie View A&M, 3 against Louisiana Tech, and 3 against Colorado, for at least 11 false starts in three home games. The Prairie View game was the low point: all four of Baylor’s false-start penalties were attributed to offensive lineman Asher Hale, and Aranda admitted afterward that one player had a bunch of penalties. Holding calls have added to the problem, but false starts are harder to excuse. ​A big reason is inexperience. The line was overhauled in the offseason and has been banged up in 2026, and while Baylor has capable players at each spot, most are new and started their first games together this year. Injuries haven’t helped either, including the injury to Koltin Sieracki, who was projected to be the best of the bunch but has not produced on the level the staff or fans expected. 5. The Bears have had a knack for getting behind the line of scrimmage this season, ranking in the top five in the nation in both sacks and tackles for loss. Who do they have to thank for that and what helps them get past offensive lines so often this season? Haddadin: The turnaround is remarkable given where this defense was a year ago. Baylor finished last season tied for last in the Big 12 and at the bottom of the FBS in sacks. Much of the credit goes to Klanderman and an offseason rebuild that put NIL money into the roster from the inside out. Defensive end Garrick Ponder leads the team with 3.5 sacks, Ryan Davis has added 2.5 off the edge, and Jordan Mack has chipped in 2.0. Up the middle, Hosea Wheeler and Traevon Mitchell occupy blockers and collapse the pocket, which opens lanes for everyone else. The most telling detail may be that two of the top three sack producers are safeties: Bo Onu and Daniel Cobbs have 3.0 sacks apiece. That says a lot about how Klanderman calls a game. He isn’t relying on one star pass rusher; six different players have at least two sacks, and he is willing to bring pressure from anywhere on the field, including the secondary. 6. What’s an aspect of this Bears team’s game that is not talked about enough? ​Haddadin: The most underrated part of this team might be the guy who comes on when the offense stalls. Senior punter Palmer Williams has quietly been one of the best weapons on the roster. He came into the year with plenty of credentials, as a 2025 All-American and Ray Guy Award finalist who earned first-team Walter Camp and second-team AP preseason All-American honors before this season. He picked up right where he left off. In the opener against Auburn, he punted four times for 208 yards, a 52-yard average, and earned Ray Guy Award Punter of the Week honors for flipping field position and helping Baylor get back into a game it nearly stole at the end. A month into the season, he was averaging over 50 yards a punt and consistently pinning punts near the goal line. He was a massive part of the win against Colorado in Week 4. As the offense struggled to move the ball, Williams flipped the field and pinned the Buffs inside their own 10-yard line on multiple occasions. If Friday’s game against UCF turns into a cagey field-position battle, Baylor won’t mind, since it has one of the best punters in the country. Turner has contributed to the Black and Gold Banneret, the home for UCF Athletics on SB Nation. He has called the Orlando area home since the age of 8 and received his bachelor's and master's degrees from UCF. (Photo by Dustin Markland/Getty Images) | Getty Images Steve Helwick Thu, October 29, 2026 at 9:12 PM UTC · 8 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads Time and date: Friday, October 30 at 7:30 p.m. ET Network: ESPN Location: Acrisure Bounce House — Orlando, FL Spread: Baylor (-1.5) Over/under: 48.5 All-time series: Baylor leads, 2-1 Last meeting: Baylor 30, UCF 3 — November 1, 2025 Current streak: Baylor, 2 (2023-25) Setting the scene Baylor and UCF have only met three times, but there is no shortage of iconic moments between these programs. UCF entered the 2013 Fiesta Bowl as a 13.5-point underdog to Big 12 champion Baylor. However, Blake Bortles led the Knights to an electrifying 52-42 victory on New Year's Day, sealing the program's first-ever AP Top 10 finish. Ten years later, UCF held a 35-7 lead in the late third quarter over Baylor, but the Bears rallied with 29 unanswered, surviving a wild fourth down conversion and a 59-yard field goal attempt to hold onto a 36-35 win. Perhaps another memorable finish awaits as the programs meet in Orlando for the 10th annual Space Game. UCF continues one of college football's most recognizable modern traditions, rebranding to the "Citronauts" for a night and donning space-themed alternate uniforms as a nod to the university's aeronautical roots. The Citronauts are one of the better teams in college football history, owning an 8-1 record in Space Games and outscoring opponents by an aggregate result of 432-189: 2017 – UCF 63, East Carolina 21 2018 – UCF 52, Temple 40 2019 – UCF 44, Houston 29 2020 – UCF 51, Tulane 34 2021 – UCF 24, Memphis 7 2022 – UCF 70, Temple 13 2023 – UCF 45, Oklahoma State 3 2024 – UCF 56, Arizona 12 2025 – Houston 30, UCF 27 However, Houston defeated UCF in last year's Space Game, spoiling the Citronauts' perfect record. UCF, coming off its first top-5 victory in program history, aims to recapture its galactic momentum as Baylor strolls into the Bounce House. Baylor Bears outlook WACO, TEXAS - SEPTEMBER 19: Defensive Coordinator Joe Klanderman of the Baylor Bears yells from the sideline during the second quarter during the game against the Louisiana Tech Bulldogs on September 19, 2026 at the McLane Stadium in Waco, Texas. (Photo by Hanna Kotlarek/Baylor Athletics/University Images via Getty Images) Baylor (4-3, 2-2 Big 12) fired head coach Dave Aranda in the middle of his seventh season in Waco. Aranda's tenure was quite volatile, featuring highs of a 12-2 finish and Big 12 championship in 2021, but lows including a 3-9 record in 2023. The Bears lacked consistency under Aranda, improving or declining by at least three wins in every year from 2019 through 2025. Baylor moves forward with interim Joe Klanderman, who also retains his defensive coordinator duties. In year one on campus, Klanderman has done a stellar job reforming Baylor's defense. He implemented a 3-3-5 base scheme and vastly improved the unit, allowing them to skyrocket from 122nd to 19th in scoring defense and 122nd to 22nd in run defense. The Bears let up just 16.1 points per game, and last Saturday's 25-24 loss to Kansas was the first time they surrendered more than 17 points all season. The defense showed promise even in losing efforts, falling 17-16 to Auburn and 17-6 to TCU. Baylor is the best in the Big 12 at getting to the quarterback and its 3.9 sacks per game rank third nationally. There isn't one dominant pass rusher, rather, it's a concerted effort. Edge rusher Garrick Ponder leads the charge with 4.0 sacks while safeties Daniel Cobbs and Bo Onu are tied for second with 3.0 apiece. With great pressure comes great chaos, and Baylor is producing takeaways at a high rate. The team ranks 15th nationally with 13 takeaways, and strong safety Micah Gifford has been omnipresent with three interceptions and two fumble recoveries. While the passing defense has more interceptions than touchdowns allowed, and forces opponents to a 59.8 completion rate, Baylor still allows 236 passing yards per game, which ranks 103rd nationally. Teams regularly hit explosives on the Bears, which have given up 13 passes of 30 yards or greater through seven games. Last season, Baylor excelled offensively and struggled on defense. This year, the opposite is true. Outside of the 55-19 rout at Arizona State, the Bears have not been able to consistently generate points. They scored 24 or fewer points in four of seven games, and all three losses were attribute to a lack of scoring. Still, quarterback DJ Lagway has moved the ball well for the nation's 24th-ranked passing offense. The veteran starter averages 270 passing yards per game, delivering nine touchdowns and four interceptions. Efficiency has been an issue through the air though, and Baylor checks in at 124th in the FBS with a 56.4 completion rate. Wide receiver Gavin Freeman operates as the main target. His 58 receptions are the second-most in the country and his 678 receiving yards rank second in the Big 12. Louis Brown and Jayden McGowan are among Lagway's other frequented options. Baylor hasn't been as lethal on the ground, still awaiting its first 90-yard rusher of the season. The Bears were held to 54 rushing yards against TCU and 122 against Kansas — a significant reason Baylor enters Orlando on a two-game losing streak. UCF Knights outlook ORLANDO, FLORIDA - OCTOBER 24: Keyone Jenkins #12 of the UCF Knights celebrates a touchdown in the first half of the game between the UCF Knights and BYU Cougars at Acrisure Bounce House on October 24, 2026 in Orlando, Florida. (Photo by Dustin Markland/Getty Images) | Getty Images UCF (4-3, 2-2 Big 12) is coming off a win for the ages. Although the Knights won multiple New Year's Six bowls and secured an NCAA-recognized national championship in 2017, last Saturday's double overtime triumph over No. 2 BYU was the program's first-ever top-5 victory in history. It was the long-awaited signature win of Scott Frost's second tenure in Orlando and restored energy into a fanbase, which will certainly show up in droves for the annual Space Game. There were moments throughout the BYU game where it appeared UCF missed a golden opportunity for an upset. However, the Knights stayed the course and won just their second October game in their last 13 tries. One of the heroes last week was quarterback Keyone Jenkins, who threw for 293 yards and three touchdowns, while rushing for an additional score in the 39-31 win. After witnessing several strong performances by the FIU transfer, Frost named Jenkins the starting quarterback moving forward, even though original starter Alonza Barnett III has recovered from a Week 2 hamstring injury. UCF has received stronger support from the passing attack in recent weeks, which has been efficient. The Knights have thrown 13 touchdowns against four interceptions, while completing 66.5 percent of attempts this year. It hasn't been the most explosive unit, completing just seven passes spanning 30 yards and two spanning 40, but Jenkins has allowed the Knights to piece together methodical possessions. The run game has been the hallmark of UCF's offense all season. Running back Duke Watson is eighth in the Big 12 in rushing and averages 6.8 yards per carry. Landen Chambers has also stepped up from the backfield lately, scoring two touchdowns in last week's win over BYU. But the true emerging star in UCF's offense is true freshman wide receiver Tyren Hornes. After being underutilized in September, Hornes has become one of the top options for the Knights, producing 137 yards on six receptions last Saturday. He now ranks second on the team in receiving yards behind Josh Derry, who leads all Knight receivers in catches (34), yards (358), and touchdowns (3). Although the last two weeks were more offensive oriented games, UCF has been best on the defensive side this year. The Knights allow 23.0 points per game, allow just 3.2 yards per rushing attempt, and hold opponents to a completion rate of 58.9 percent. However, UCF must play the Space Game without arguably its best defensive player. Strong safety Demari Henderson suffered an injury in overtime against BYU, and the team will miss his production, which includes 35 tackles, two interceptions, and five pass breakups. The Knights still have several veteran faces in the secondary including cornerbacks Antione Jackson and Jayden Bellamy, who both have one interception and one forced fumble on the season. Thanks to these defensive backs, UCF is a plus-5 in the turnover battle this season. Can UCF avoid a letdown after an emotional win? Signature wins haven't been easy to follow up in college football this season. Auburn beat Georgia and then lost by 21 to LSU at home. BYU took down Notre Dame and then dropped an overtime thriller to UCF a week later. Ole Miss' triumph over LSU was followed by a thrashing at the hands of Florida. And so on. Baylor also had an eventful week, as the Bears move on from head coach Dave Aranda and now must respond with an interim head coach in a hostile Orlando environment. The Bears' defense has been consistently sound this year, and UCF may struggle to come close to its Space Game average of 48 points per game. The defenses control this matchup, and the Bears prevent a successful launch with a game-winning field goal in the final minute. Prediction: Baylor 24, UCF 21

Pete Fiutak Thu, October 29, 2026 at 2:02 AM UTC · 3 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads Here's the punchline – both Baylor and UCF are 4-3 overall and 2-2 in Big 12 play. On one side, Baylor lost on the road to Kansas in a 25-24 fight, and that was it. Head coach Dave Aranda was fired, defensive coordinator Joe Klanderman is the interim head man, and the team needs this win with a tough November coming up. However, win in Orlando, beat Iowa State at home, and boom – the Bears are bowl-eligible. UCF lost on the road to Houston and Oklahoma State, and then it changed the national landscape – and got Scott Frost his first huge win in his second round with the Knights – with a 39-31 victory over BYU. With a very favorable finishing kick, UCF has to keep the momentum going. Baylor vs UCF: Quick Hits Baylor has the home date against Iowa State next, and then there's a problem – at BYU, Texas Tech, at Houston. UCF goes to Kansas after this, and then plays Arizona State, Iowa State, and goes to Colorado. None of those four are likely to go to a bowl game. It's the fourth meeting between the two. Baylor won 30-3 last year and won 36-35 in 2023, but UCF won a wild 52-42 Fiesta Bowl to end the 2013 season. How To Watch Baylor vs UCF Date: Friday, October 30, 2026 Game Time: 7:30 PM ET TV: ESPN Location: Acrisure Bounce House, Orlando, FL – Week 9 Schedule, Game Previews – CFN Top 25 | Bowl Projections – Predicting the First CFP Top 25 – CFN Week 9 Expert Picks Why Baylor Will Win The defense is taking the ball away in bunches. The run defense has been fantastic – Kansas ripped it up last week, but that was an anomaly – but the takeaways have been the biggest help, with 13 overall and at least two in four games. UCF doesn't have to get the running game going to win, but it's a huge help going 4-1 when running for more than 100 yards. Baylor has held four teams to under 100, but … Why UCF Will Win UCF isn't having a problem with turnovers. It has only given it up seven times, didn't turn it over against BYU, and it's +5 overall in turnover margin. So really, how did UCF beat BYU? The running game was effective enough – even if it wasn't dominant – and the passing game was fearless, and that's how the Knights have to play. They don't have to bomb away, but they should take the midrange plays against a Baylor pass defense that can get to the quarterback but is susceptible to quick hits. Baylor vs UCF Prediction, Betting Lines UCF needs to capitalize on the momentum, and it will. The Knights are 4-0 in the Bounce House, and 0-3 away from it. Baylor hung 55 at Arizona State and suffered two one-point losses away from Waco, but now it has to deal with the coaching drama and all the changes. The team will play hard and well for Klanderman, but the UCF offense will be just a bit more effective.
