away.headline: 5 Questionable Decisions That Defined Dave Aranda's Baylor Tenure
away.blurb: 5 Questionable Decisions That Defined Dave Aranda's Baylor Tenure Skip to main content SI.COM Here are five of the most questionable decisions of Aranda's Baylor tenure. Aranda had reason to overhaul Baylor's defensive staff following the 2022 season, but his choice of replacement proved questionable. Continuing to direct the defense while overseeing the entire program raised questions about whether Aranda had taken on too much. Although his defensive expertise was never in doubt, the arrangement potentially limited the attention he could devote to recruiting, roster construction and other head coaching duties. Dave Aranda's tenure at Baylor peaked in 2021, when the Bears won a program-record 12 games, captured the Big 12 championship and claimed a Sugar Bowl victory. Nearly five years later, he was fired following Saturday's 25-24 loss at Kansas, finishing his six-plus seasons in Waco with a 40-40 record. Baylor's decline can't be traced to a single mistake, but several of Aranda's decisions played a role in the program's inability to sustain its success. Some made sense at the time but ultimately backfired, while others were mistakes he later acknowledged. 1. Aranda's emphasis on player development helped establish the culture behind Baylor's 2021 championship, but that same philosophy arguably kept the Bears from adapting quickly enough to college football's changing roster landscape. Baylor added only 10 scholarship transfers during Aranda's first three seasons before bringing in 12 during the 2023 cycle. While other programs increasingly used the portal to address immediate needs, the Bears remained more reliant on developing players already on their roster. Aranda later acknowledged struggling with bringing in transfers when doing so could mean passing over players he had recruited and developed. That reluctance became particularly costly following the 2021 season, when Baylor lost several important contributors, including Jalen Pitre, JT Woods, Terrel Bernard and Abram Smith. Replacing that experience and production was never going to be easy, but the transfer portal offered opportunities to address weaknesses before they became bigger problems. Instead, Baylor struggled to maintain the depth and physicality that had helped it win the conference championship. home.blurb: Coach Scott Frost said running back Taevion Swint will be back quickly, and linebacker Lewis Carter could be a game-time decision this week . He added that if the senior isn't available against the Baylor Bears, he'll likely be a game-time decision next Saturday against the Kansas Jayhawks . Carter has missed every conference game this season. He went into the medical tent for a knee injury at the end of Week 3's win over the Georgia State Panthers and was ruled out early for the next game. More Videos The UCF Knights made program history in upsetting the then-No. 2 BYU Cougars , and a few key players are on the cusp of returning for Friday's Space Game. Swint's injury occurred in practice, and Frost said he started limping after a "nothing play." The redshirt freshman missed his first game of the season , leaving room for Landen Chambers to step up in his absence. UCF has relied on the speedster to make plays in the run game and on special teams. Swint's rushed for 162 yards and two touchdowns on 32 carries, and returned seven kickoffs for 209 yards. He scored his first touchdown in the season opener against the Bethune-Cookman Wildcats, and the second in the Big 12 home opener against the TCU Horned Frogs . The Knights have missed their defensive quarterback, especially in highly contested losses against the then-No. 20 Houston Cougars and then-No. 18 Oklahoma State Cowboys . The senior had a career season last year after transferring from Oklahoma . Carter led the team with 92 tackles and set career highs in tackles for loss, sacks, and fumbles. He became a star at UCF. While at Oklahoma, he was a reserve linebacker and special teams player. Wisconsin transfer Tackett Curtis, the team's leading tackler, has stepped up in Carter's absence. Curtis has 42 tackles (18 solo, 24 assisted), one sack, one fumble recovery, one pass deflection and two interceptions. The Knights are getting healthy at the right time. They aim to build on an upset win and collect two more wins to break a two-year bowl drought. Friday's game against Baylor is one of the more interesting weekday matchups . The program fired coach David Aranda, and Joe Klanderman is the interim coach. UCF's eight-game Space Game winning streak ended in heartbreaking fashion as Houston caught the game-winning interception against former Knights quarterback Davi Belfort. home.headline: BYU vs. UCF injury report: Two players listed for Cougars
home.blurb: Running back LJ Martin is listed as out, while starting offensive guard Kyle Sfarcioc is questionable. Running back Sione Moa and safety Tommy Prassas are both expected to be available for the game. One is running back LJ Martin , the 2025 Big 12 Offensive Player of the Year. ESPN's Pete Thamel reported that he'd miss 4-6 weeks after the TCU game, meaning he has roughly 2-4 weeks remaining on that diagnosis. That injury was expected, as Martin is listed as "Out." Starting offensive guard Kyle Sfarcioc is the other Cougar listed on the injury report, as he has a "Questionable" designation going into the game. BYU's offensive line has been one of the nation's best, with Sfarcioc a big part of it. He missed the game against Notre Dame, and the Cougars handled his absence very well in giving quarterback Bear Bachmeier ample time to throw. But getting back the 6-foot-4, 305-pound redshirt senior would provide another boost to this group, one they might need against a pesky UCF defense. On the other side, the Knights have six players listed as out, one listed as doubtful, three listed as questionable and six listed as probable. The BYU Cougars will soon take the field to match up against the UCF Knights in a Week 8 Big 12 matchup, with the game kicking off at 1:00 p.m. MT on Saturday. And in that game, the Cougars will be very healthy. In the latest injury report, the Cougars have just two players listed. Also of note is that running back Sione Moa is not on the injury report, as he suffered an injury against Utah Tech in the season-opener and was sidelined — up until this week, it seems. He was cleared to play against Notre Dame, but wasn't a go for confidence reasons, offensive coordinator Aaron Roderick told reporters. Safety Tommy Prassas, the team's third-leading tackler (23), is also a full-go after dealing with his own injury.
